Medication and Therapy Management

Sometimes, anxiety can be intentional to require some kind of medication to control its symptoms. Along with therapy, medication works very well in a very holistic manner. This combined approach often brings faster and more lasting relief.

h1: What are the Signs of a Mental Health Issue?
excerpt: Understanding the Early Signs of Mental Health Issues Mental health challenges often begin in silence – with subtle changes and tricking patterns that can easily be seen as a phase. But just like any other physical illness, mental health issues also have some signs and symptoms that should not be ignored. Recognising that early can […]
contentHtml:
Understanding the Early Signs of Mental Health Issues

Mental health challenges often begin in silence – with subtle changes and tricking patterns that can easily be seen as a phase. But just like any other physical illness, mental health issues also have some signs and symptoms that should not be ignored. Recognising that early can make a big difference when it comes to recovery and maintaining long-term well-being.  Let’s discuss some key points that can suggest that someone is drifting towards a mental health slump and is struggling with the same.

  • – Persistent Changes in Mood and Changed Behaviour

When somebody shows frequent sadness or irritability and just seems out of their character for a long period of time, it is time to consider a soft approach. When a person’s mood remains slow or unstable for a long time, it is a thing to be concerned about friends and family might notice this in an instant as the loved ones remain isolated and become unusually reactive to small things.

  • – Difficulty Managing Daily Tasks

Any organised person may start missing their deadlines, neglecting, rare, personal hygiene or even withdrawing from activities they once enjoyed. Small daily responsibilities can begin to feel overwhelming. This happens usually when under chronic stress and the person is on the edge of burnout can cause issues, anxiety, depression disorders as well.

  • – Sleep and Appetite Changes

Sleep is the major area that takes a hit when it comes to mental health issues. According to our conversations with a psychiatrist in Noida, insomnia, restless nights, and excessive sleeping are all big warning signs. Changes in appetite are also major indicators. Eating too much or too little can also signal emotional distress.

Both the body and the mind reflect imbalance through these major metabolic activities.

  • – Physical Symptoms without Clear Cause

Headaches, body, pain, fatigue, or digestive issues that persist without any cause are also linked to psychological stress. The body sees what the mind suppresses. This is a strong reminder that mental health and physical health are deeply connected.

  • – Difficulty Concentrating on Making Decisions

Mental health struggles can cloud focus and decision making skills. The mind may feel forgetful or foggy at times. The symptom is often overlooked, but it’s a significant sign of mental struggle.

If you know someone who shows several of these signs, reach out to a psychiatrist in Noida who can provide a proper diagnosis and treatment plan. Early intervention is the key to preventing conditions from worship and supporting long-term recovery.

It contributes to more swings, fatigue, and depressive symptoms.

A list of important nutrients like vitamin B12, four, zinc, and magnesium play an essential in regulating mood. A deficiency in these can lead to symptoms that mimic and worse, depression. Conversely, Mediterranean style diets like the FODMAP diet have been linked to lower rates of depression and anxiety.

title: What Is It Like to Live with Antisocial Personality Disorder?
h1: What Is Antisocial Personality Disorder?
excerpt: What Is Antisocial Personality Disorder? Feeling like a misfit in their own circle, Antisocial personality disorder is a complex condition. Here, a person is constantly misunderstood and misinterpreted by their peers and caregivers for their actions and behaviours. At its core, antisocial personality disorder is seen as a disorder where a person does not care […]
contentHtml:
Feeling like a misfit in their own circle, Antisocial personality disorder is a complex condition. Here,  a person is constantly misunderstood and misinterpreted by their peers and caregivers for their actions and behaviours. 

At its core, antisocial personality disorder is seen as a disorder where a person does not care about others rights, feels impulsive, has deceitful actions and lacks remorse about it. Although pathologically described like this, the clinical description actually does not describe how it feels for a person to live with this condition.

Research Backed Evidences

Contrary to popular belief, people with APD tend to understand emotional and interpersonal experiences according to the Journal of Personality disorders. They could not actually relate to emotions and felt a detachment from usual norms that dictated emotions. This shows that they understand the rules intellectually, but do not interact with their emotional aspects properly.

This emotional deregulation establishes the main component of antisocial personality. Another research in the American Journal of Psychiatry talked about the neurological problems of antisocial personality. Here it showed that people with antisocial personality lack impulse control and emotional regulation because of issues in their amygdala  and prefrontal cortex. This shows that this disorder also has a neurological basis of functioning.

Living with Antisocial Personality Disorder

Living with antisocial personality disorder can be quite isolating as well as challenging. This challenge is supposed to both the affected person and the people that live around them. Usually, it occurs due to some kind of trauma, response, disrupted attachments, and conflicts in relationships. People feel many issues arise when they try to form meaningful social connections like relationships, friendships, and romantic connections. 

Such people also tend to engage in harmful behaviours that aim to manipulate and hurt others in an emotional and physical manner.

Treatment Options Available

Treatment options here remain very limited due to lack of research, but usually structured therapy works best. Therapeutic options can include cognitive behavioural therapy, dialectical behavioural therapy, and other interventions like medications and group therapy to manage symptoms. All these therapies are able to manage the emotional issues that arise during the course of the disorder and provide long-term relief. 

With such insights, people are able to understand what a person goes through during this disorder and are able to fetch help that is more supportive, understanding and holistic. With our team at Tulasi Healthcare, experts understand your dilemma and provide a source of compassion and hope to all.

excerpt: What Causes Histrionic Personality Disorder? Histrionic personality disorder is a type of disorder that is seen as a pattern of Seeking constant attention without any need of it. Such individuals feel uncomfortable when they are not the centre of attention and can use any means necessary to draw it back to themselves. Acts like maintaining […]
contentHtml:
Histrionic personality disorder is a type of disorder that is seen as a pattern of Seeking constant attention without any need of it. Such individuals feel uncomfortable when they are not the centre of attention and can use any means necessary to draw it back to themselves. Acts like maintaining their physical appearance, expressions, behaviour, or seduction are their common acts. They are not drawn by emotions, rather their emotions are rapidly shifting, but can seem intense. Their mindset are quite superficial and focused on the current situation.

The core of this disorder lies in approval and validation from the other person. They can be very charming individuals, indeed, but suffer from struggling relationships throughout their lives. Since their emotional bonds cannot last, they cannot relate to the intimacy of relationships as much. Dealing with historic personality disorder as a therapist or as a family member can be challenging. It can require empathy, boundaries and patients to start a treatment plan.

Set Clear Boundaries

People with this disorder push limits to draw attention to themselves during therapy. Setting these boundaries and emotional behaviours can help them keep their relationships healthy. If we avoid using dramatic behaviours to replicate their behaviour, this helps them reinforce calm and communication.

Avoid Criticism and Power Struggle

When such people are criticised, they do not take it well. It can result in emotional outburst and defensiveness. Instead of challenging them, asking them clarifying questions again and again to define their behaviour can be a great way to ground them. This helps them reflect on their own behaviour.

Encourage Therapy

Cognitive behavioural therapy is considered one of the best for his historic personality treatment. It helps individuals identify their adaptive behaviour and become more and more aware of it. This therapy helps them identify their emotional expression, improve their interpersonal skills and remove the impulsivity to secret attention. According to the Journal of personality disorders, people with historic personality disorder usually respond to structured and gold oriented therapy. 

Recognising Emotional Needs

Behind every maladaptive behaviour, their lies, an emotional lead that is yet unfulfilled. It can be a result of validation or fear of abandonment. Instead of feeling frustrated, approaching interactions with empathy and insight can be much more helpful. 

Dealing with historic personality disorder is not about changing the person all together – it is about changing and knowing their emotional needs. When healthier dynamic steps in- treatment can be fulfilled. Connect with Tulasi Healthcare today to know more on this disorder.

contentHtml:
Obsessive compulsive disorder is quite often misunderstood by people who have no knowledge of it. It is simply seen as an urge to clean up and keep things in order without looking at the intricacies it holds. In reality, it is a very serious mental health condition where people indulge into obsession and repetitive behaviours to alleviate their anxiety from maladaptive thoughts. For many living with this condition can feel like a loop of endless thoughts and behaviours. Tackling this can be a challenge, but surely people with this condition can live a happy life if given proper intervention and measurements in time. 

Despite the challenges, this is possible. While this condition does not disappear overnight – it is highly treatable. Seeking the right support strategy and mindset with Tulasi Healthcare can help you gain a happy functioning life.

The Role of Treatment

The most effective treatment plans usually are the most simplest. Cognitive behavioural therapy and exposure in response prevention are usually the required methods to generate the best results. The gradual exposure to the stimulus helps in relieving anxiety and helping them resist the urge. Over time, the compulsion feels more like a regular act and helps them regain control over their lives. According to the Journal of the American Medical Association, ERP has a significant impact on the issues of OCD and highly improves the quality of life. 

The medications like selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are also quite helpful when combined with therapy. 

Beyond Symptom Management

Living with obsessive compulsive disorder is not just about reducing the symptoms that come with it. It is also about building a life with purpose and function. Practices like mindfulness, self compassion and creative outlets, help in long-term management of the symptoms. 

A research from Clinical Psychology Review  supports the use of acceptance and commitment therapy. It fosters the acceptance of maladaptive thoughts and building upon them in a positive manner. A shift in perspective is needed to foster resilience, understanding, and hope along with emotional flexibility.

Obsessive compulsive disorder is a part of a person’s life. It can neither be redacted fully or be accepted for its flaws. The right treatment comes from understanding it and living meaningful, joyful lives with continuous efforts and interventions. title: What are the Signs of a Narcissist Person?
h1: Understanding the Signs of a Narcissist
excerpt: Understanding the Signs of a Narcissist We often use the word narcissist very casually in our conversations, but in psychology, it holds a very different meaning. If you’re talking about a person with narcissistic personality disorder, it becomes something very deeper and very serious. NPD is a real mental health condition where a person shows […]
contentHtml:
We often use the word narcissist very casually in our conversations, but in psychology, it holds a very different meaning. If you’re talking about a person with narcissistic personality disorder, it becomes something very deeper and very serious. NPD is a real mental health condition where a person shows long-term patterns of self-importance, need to see attention at all times, and little to no empathy for others. 

According to the American Journal of psychiatry, there are many types of narcissist that exist like grandiose, vulnerable, and high functioning variants. But they all share some common characteristics.

There are some common signs that can be spotted easily with the eye and accurate knowledge about the disorder. With this in mind, let’s look at the signs in a simple way.

– They think very highly of themselves– usually a narcissist believes that they are very special. They believe that they should have perfect lives, relationships and stories. Their desire is always to be admired and become powerful in their lives.

– They have unreal fantasies– a perfect life is a utopian idea, which most narcissists tend to believe in. Their ideas are not backed by reality.

– They feel they are unique – They critically feel themselves to be unique or special. It marks a very crucial point of being a narcissist because they believe only special people can understand them and do not like to be in ordinary spaces or situations. Their ideas, behaviours and actions are all out of the ordinary to indicate this.

– Constantly seek praise – Narcissists always feel that they should be admired, even when the situation or the condition is not about them. If not so, they feel out of place, uncomfortable and upset. Their self-worth usually depends on what others think and feel about them.

– Expecting special treatment– Such people usually believe that rules are not for them, but for everybody else. They feel that they deserve extra attention all the time and special favors without any need for it.

– They tend to take advantage of others– Since they have a big emotional disconnect, such people do not feel deeply when they take advantage of others or when others feel hurt by them. 

Narcissism, as reflected by the above points goes beyond these in subtle actions and behaviours. It is a deep need to feel accepted, while forming healthy relationships in the way. If pointed at the right time, seeking treatment and long-term functionality is possible for people with narcissistic personality disorder. If you know someone who is exhibiting the signs and might need help for the same, providing support and assistance can be crucial. When it comes to finding a solution through the expert opinion, talking to a good psychiatrist in India can be a great way to approach the issue. As for the treatment insights, there is one that stands out in all aspects- Cognitive Behavioral Therapy. 

CBT has the highest efficacy rate for most mental disorders. So, let’s discover how CBT treats anxiety with some scientific support.

How is CBT Effective?

CBT is a short term and a goal oriented therapy plan that focuses on changing the negative thought process to bring about behavioral change. It is based on the idea that our thoughts, feelings and behaviors are all connected to each other and a change in one influences the other. 

1. For someone with anxiety, it might be like this: Challenging a thought like- “If this happens then what will I do?”

2. Replacing them with rational thoughts like- “This is uncomfortable  but I can take care of it.”

3. Practicing behaviors that stabilise our minds.

When Research Speaks for Effectiveness?

A metanalysis published in Cognitive Therapy & Research showed that CBT is highly effective in treating mental health issues like Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Panic Disorder and Social Anxiety Disorder.

Another study published in Lancet Psychiatry showed that CBT is even more effective than Placebo, when provided by a trained expert like any psychiatrist in India with legitimate certifications and experience.

How are the sessions structured?

The sessions are quite structured and conducted weekly or as needed. They follow a pattern as shown:

– Identify negative thoughts that spring up automatically

– Challenge irrational beliefs and thoughts

– Practicing coping skills that arm us in real life situations

– Engage in exposure exercises. 

CBT is more than a therapy- it is a tool for people to identify where they lack in their beliefs and build strong ones through expert intervention. With Dr. Gorav Gupta, one can find a way to live a fulfilling life that builds on wellbeing with therapies like CBT. excerpt: How Group Therapy Works: The 4 Stages Explained Whatever experiences we have in our lifetimes are not limited to ourselves- they may be personal in some aspects but do share some commonalities with others. When we look at our experiences from a broader perspective, they build on some common principles. This binds us to many […]
contentHtml:
Whatever experiences we have in our lifetimes are not limited to ourselves- they may be personal in some aspects but do share some commonalities with others. When we look at our experiences from a broader perspective, they build on some common principles. This binds us to many suffering from negative ones, providing us hope and a will to move past them. Wellbeing is not only the presence of happy moments and physical fitness- it is also the presence of resilience and ability to move beyond negativity. 

From the lens of an expert like a psychiatrist, it is easy to understand this perspective. Group Therapy is a great tool to understand the grand perspective of your issues and find a solution through them. Many psychologist in Delhi and experts throughout the country firmly believe in the efficacy of this therapy. 

Let’s understand the different stages that are employed in Group Therapy that help in therapeutic interventions:

1. Forming- Finding Your Place

This is the first stage. Here participants feel anxious and struggle to find their place in the group. They are polite yet hesitate to see their place being formed in the closed structure. A good psychiatrist will make sure that each individual involved finds what they need and adjust to the current condition. An early study published in the International Journal of Group Psychotherapy focused on creating psychological safety for participants in the early stages of therapy.This led to good long term outcomes.

2. Storming- Navigating Differences

As people start opening up, they might find certain differences and feel that they don’t belong in the group. Members may even go ahead and challenge their peers and therapist to find a way out. This is where a trained professional steps in. If you have ever approached a psychologist in Delhi, they will try their best to inculcate better practices and help you adjust in the group.

3. Norming- Building Trust

Gradually, the clients start to understand the norms of the group and adjust to the process. This leads them to open up and develop a community based on their issues and solutions shared. This directive leads to a good cohesion and solution seeking practice.

4. Performing- Growth & Reflection

This is the phase that offers transformation. Members begin to discuss and apply their insights in real life. They may share how these insights have impacted them in real life and helped them manage crises in difficult situations. 

Group Therapy is a journey filled with silence to sharing. It builds a practice to share insights that can help others find a solution and expression in real life. With Tulasi Healthcare, you find a solution that helps you build wellbeing in long-term.

title: What is the Goal of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy?
h1: Understanding the Goal of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
excerpt: Understanding the Goal of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Acceptance and Commitment- these are the two words that people usually have a hard time understanding and applying in real life. There are many situations and issues that can land them in this, and it is not easy for them to fully accept its repercussions and move […]
contentHtml:
Acceptance and Commitment- these are the two words that people usually have a hard time understanding and applying in real life. There are many situations and issues that can land them in this, and it is not easy for them to fully accept its repercussions and move forward. There are many instances in life where we mourn with grief and loss, marry, leave our near and dear ones or face a sudden change in life. Sometimes, we are ready for these decisions, but it may happen that they have a severe impact on our psyche. 

Acceptance and Commitment Therapy deals in the same principle. Knowing what lies ahead and making peace with the situation is a practical way to live that many might not know. Here, this therapy has a huge role to play. It changes the way we deal with our anxiety, depression and stress with the help of a psychiatrist or a psychologist. If you are a resident of Delhi NCR region, you can find some of the top psychologist in Delhi to share your concerns with.

Accepting- Not Avoiding

ACT encourages people to make peace with their negative emotions, unlike other therapies which aim to eradicate them. Difficult emotions need to be there for us to assess the positives that linger with it. It teaches people to sit with their thoughts and accept the things as they are, and commit to finding a solution to them.

A study published in Behavior Research and Therapy showed that it is highly effective in treating anxiety disorders, particularly reducing avoidance behaviors.

Living with Your Values

Another core value that drives ACT is committed action towards your inner values. There are motivations and values that drive our thoughts and behaviors. With this therapy, we can take steps in the positive direction by continually committing to our positive actions. 

As per a study published in Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, ACT significantly improves efficacy for treatment of PTSD, depression and anxiety. With this, come long term benefits and along with medication, it has high positive turnouts.

In daily life, it helps people notice their thoughts and act on them in real time. It is not just a therapy, but a continued aspect of their intrapersonal learning and improvement.

If you are looking to find guidance with this therapy for your issues, consulting a psychologist in Delhi or a psychiatrist might be a great way to start. Connect with Tulasi Healthcare today to find a path towards wellbeing.

title: Tips to Get Out of Depression
h1: How to Manage Depression Naturally
excerpt: How to Manage Depression Naturally We all have had times where we feel down, don’t feel the need to work or just sit idly by. Some days, it may feel normal- everybody faces the ebb and flow of life. But when these lows start to f stay on our minds for a long period of […]
contentHtml:
We all have had times where we feel down, don’t feel the need to work or just sit idly by. Some days, it may feel normal- everybody faces the ebb and flow of life. But when these lows start to f stay on our minds for a long period of time, it is not a good sign. When even simple tasks begin to look big, it may be time to evaluate our lifestyle and wellbeing. These shape our mindsets and behavior, and it’s important to know that there is something we can do about it. 

Depression is a very common mental health condition- which can be very hard to deal with without any motivation. Having some tips to easily manage from the lens of an expert like a psychiatrist can help people easily steer through their issues. Tips for lifestyle management are essential in such cases- so let’s explore some.

Start Where You are be Kind to Yourself

While dealing with depression, the level of motivation being low is a quite common symptom. The feeling of being depressed can bring about a series of issues, so it is necessary to be kind to oneself while dealing with it. If you are consulting with a psychiatrist in Delhi, they will have many practical tips of action to share for depression, from which being kind to yourself holds a high regard.

Talk to Someone

Talking to a friend or someone you feel comfortable with can be a way to share your negative feelings. Knowing that you have someone who is open to your concerns is a comfort. An honest conversation helps you break the loop of negative thinking, as described by some top psychiatrist in Delhi. Reaching out can definitely feel terrifying, but it’s the first step to assuring your wellbeing. 

Create a Routine

This may sound like a very simple activity, but it’s one of the core steps of moving towards first line management of depression. During depressive episodes, a person may not be motivated to carry out even some of the very simple day to day tasks. This can render them out of routine. Creating a small routine- even getting out of bed, brushing and making a small breakfast can work wonders.

Having a routine creates a sense of achievement, which provides motivation. Something small and consistent is something that is necessary to keep the mind going. As a top psychiatrist in Delhi for depression, Dr. Gorav Gupta fully supports these practices and applies them in his holistic development programs.

Exercise and Move Around

People usually undermine the efficacy of exercising daily and keeping the body active. It is a crucial part of our lifestyle that is seldom ignored from our lives. Exercising can be a game changer for depression. But let’s be a little honest here- getting a suggestion to go out and run when you are in the middle of an emotional slump seems a little insensitive. Here, exercising does not mean doing heavy workouts and indulging in grueling sessions. It can simply be the presence of activity in the body, something that gets you going. Put on some music, dance to the beats, stretch around and giving your body a little space to rejuvenate is something magical. 

According to some of the best psychiatrist in Delhi, exercising adds a lot of energy and a holistic aspect to healing. Since this activity produces dopamine and serotonin in the body, it is also scientifically backed to retain its efficacy.

See and Eat with Mindfulness

Dietary habits and lifestyle shape an awful lot around us than we can imagine. It has the power to either build our life or ruin it in the long run. These habits shape our mindset, thoughts and behavior. Endless scrolling and taking an unhealthy diet can have a deteriorating effect on our lives. 

Simply indulging in good eating habits, taking a nutritious balanced diet and consuming positive and mindful content can work wonders. In one’s journey from depression to wellbeing, these play a simple but core role.

Get Professional help without Hesitation

Professional help is necessary when things seem to spiral out of control. If you feel things are slipping out of hand even after taking the best measures, it is important to seek help. Any psychiatrist in Delhi or in your region can help you assess your symptoms and provide an accurate diagnosis. Professional help ensures that you are in supervision and are receiving the best of care. 

Reaching out and taking steps towards wellbeing are acts of care and self-compassion. Don’t let stigma and judgement hold you back from doing what is right for you.

title: What are the 4 domains of Interpersonal Therapy?
h1: Understanding the 4 Core Domains of Interpersonal Therapy
excerpt: Understanding the 4 Core Domains of Interpersonal Therapy Human Beings are social animals. Our survival depends upon making connections and thriving through those emotional insights. As a therapeutic method, Interpersonal Therapy helps people fulfill the need of their emotional saturation. IPT is rooted in one core principle- individuals thrive on interpersonal relationships. How we connect, […]
contentHtml:
Human Beings are social animals. Our survival depends upon making connections and thriving through those emotional insights. As a therapeutic method, Interpersonal Therapy helps people fulfill the need of their emotional saturation. IPT is rooted in one core principle- individuals thrive on interpersonal relationships. How we connect, communicate and cope with others sets the path of our lives. Our contentment, stability and balance depends upon these connections. A seasoned psychologist in Delhi once explained, ‘The issue of unresolved problems is not just within your mind; it also resides in conversations, losses and tensions that remain within your interpersonal relations.’ If you approach a psychiatrist, you might be looking at a mix of therapies that they will apply to help you resolve your issues, depending upon the details. 

IPT is one of the most crucial therapies, applying a very fundamental aspect of life to enhance wellbeing. Let’s know what are the 4 important domains that uphold interpersonal therapy.

What Exactly is IPT?

IPT is a psychological therapy that is used to improve an individual’s state of mind through analysing and resolving interpersonal interactions. It focuses on 4 core domains- which are based on the fact that most emotional issues reside within these domains.

1. Grief and Loss

This domain deals with the death of a loved and close one, which starts a downward emotional spiral for most of us. If the mourning becomes long and complicated, it can lead to serious mental health issues. According to a study published in the American Journal of Psychiatry, IPT is highly effective in treating major depression, which is usually the case when a person suffers from profound grief and loss.

2. Role Disputes

Conflicts with parents, partners, friends, peers and colleagues fall within this category. IPT steps in as a measure for these individuals to organize their roles and resolve their disputes and move towards a healthier communication pattern.

3. Role Transitions

This stems from the new changes in a person’s life like changing jobs, parenthood, getting married or divorcing. Here, a person may feel a sense of emotional disbalance and might take time to reach a level of harmony with their environment. IPT helps people step into their new roles while having compassion for themselves and others. 

As any top psychologist in Delhi can confirm, these changes are quite real and can be dealt with by just having some compassion for oneself.

4. Interpersonal Deficit

The deficits refer to the problems in making and maintaining new relationships.IPT helps build social skills, improve confidence, and create emotional connections.

 If you approach any psychiatrist with these issues, they can help you out in recognizing your patterns and providing alternative solutions through IPT.

title: What does Exposure Therapy Do?
h1: How Exposure Therapy Works?
excerpt: How Exposure Therapy Works? Some people face such traumatic instances in their lives that it leaves a deep mark on their psyche. This leaves them with a psychological scar that can take a lifetime to remove. Phobias, Panic Attacks and trauma triggers- all of these can be resolved through a revolutionary practice- Exposure Therapy. It […]
contentHtml:
Some people face such traumatic instances in their lives that it leaves a deep mark on their psyche. This leaves them with a psychological scar that can take a lifetime to remove. Phobias, Panic Attacks and trauma triggers- all of these can be resolved through a revolutionary practice- Exposure Therapy. It is a powerful treatment designed to help people face their fears, get rid of them- not avoid them and house them in their memory.

If you have ever wondered how people successfully overcome their phobias and fears, chances are that exposure therapy is involved crucially in the process.

What is Exposure Therapy in Principle?

The principle of exposure therapy lies in the name itself- gradual exposure to the fearful situation where the responses are moulded into positive ones. Although the client is exposed, it is done in a safe, controlled and therapeutic setting under the supervision of a psychiatrist. If you are looking for this therapy in the Delhi-NCR region, a good psychologist in Gurugram can also help you.

For example, a person has a fear of public speaking where they feel extremely fearful of facing any kind of crowd. This is where a psychiatrist steps in. With a structured approach, they help the clients face their fears in small steps. Eventually stepping up the difficulty with each session, they build exposure through imagination practice, then through audio and video, then eventually focusing on actual public speaking.

What Research Says

Social Anxiety Disorder has seen a high level of treatment efficacy with Exposure Therapy (The Lancet Psychiatry). It has seen higher performance levels than medications in some cases. Another meta analysis in the Journal of Anxiety Disorders indicated that exposure therapy is one of the most effective therapy for phobias, PTSD and panic disorders. It also has very low relapse rates with long lasting effects, according to some of the best psychologist in Gurgaon.

Avoidance may feel like protection sometimes, but it cannot serve you well in the long run. Over time, it engraves itself in the mind and memory, causing significant trouble. title: What is the REBT Approach to Therapy?
h1: What is the REBT Approach to Therapy?
excerpt: REBT Therapy: What It Is and How It Can Help You Changing decades of mindset is a hard task. Even as an adolescent, it takes effort to move out of a set pattern of thoughts, emotions and behaviors. Developed by Dr. Albert Ellis in 1950’s, Rational Emotive Behavioral Therapy is one of the first evolving […]
contentHtml:
REBT Therapy: What It Is and How It Can Help You

Changing decades of mindset is a hard task. Even as an adolescent, it takes effort to move out of a set pattern of thoughts, emotions and behaviors. Developed by Dr. Albert Ellis in 1950’s, Rational Emotive Behavioral Therapy is one of the first evolving forms of CBT. One of the most effective and efficacy focused therapies is REBT. It is an effective tool that is used to transform thoughts and habits that have been engraved in the behaviors through active reconstruction. It is still a highly relevant therapy since its inception- tackling issues of the fast moving urban lives. 

How REBT Works

Beliefs, emotions and actions- these are the pillars of REBT that act on our behaviors and mindset. The basic idea is very simple- it is not the events that directly affect us- it is the kind of belief that we hold towards it that shapes its existence in our lives. REBT employs the ABC model:

A– Activating Event

B– Belief

C– Consequence

If you approach a psychiatrist or any psychologist in Delhi for intervention, the next steps of the therapy jump into action. 

D– The psychiatrist helps the client disrupt these thoughts and understand what is happening

E– The ‘Effect’ of these thoughts and irrational beliefs is analyzed with a combined effort of the therapist and the client

F– With this belief and new found realization, the client forms new thoughts and coping mechanisms for irrational thoughts and behaviors.

After an in-depth assessment of different clients through many years, some of the best psychologist in Delhi talk about the life changing behaviors that come with REBT.

Research Based Evidence

REBT is not just a philosophical aspect- it’s a proven effort. The Journal of Clinical Psychology indicates that REBT significantly impacts the treatment for anxiety, depression and anger disorders.  Another study published in the European Journal of Psychotherapy and Counselling provided an insight that it helps in building long term resilience. It encourages rational and flexible thinking.

REBT is incredibly empowering in the face of thinking & behaving differently by feeling better. It encourages the right kind of support- and this is where mental wellbeing begins. With Tulasi Healthcare- move towards your wellbeing today.

excerpt: Understanding DBT Therapy: What It Is and How It Works Experiencing emotional and behavioral changes can be some of the most trying times of an individual’s life. contentHtml:
Experiencing emotional and behavioral changes can be some of the most trying times of an individual’s life. Such changes bring about instability and doubt, which can have a great impact on daily and long term functioning. This debilitating situation is something that sadly many get to experience. With the new advancements in therapeutic modalities, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy has opened doors that can converge healing with emotional stability. Originally employed by Dr. Marsha Linehan for treating Borderline Personality Disorder, DBT has proven effective in many ways for treating other mental health conditions.

Let’s discuss how this therapy works and add to the therapeutic modalities today.

Balancing Acceptance and Change

At the core, DBT helps people find the right balance between their emotions and feelings. This helps them identify their rationality and logical reasoning in times of highly emotional situations, It helps them move towards a meaningful change  while understanding their own needs.Unlike other therapies, it is employed by a psychiatrist since it is structured and skill based. As per some of the best psychologist in Gurugram, it is a great tool to gain control in situations of emotional outbursts and alter behavior significantly.

It has 4 core components that include

– Mindfulness

– Stress Tolerance

– Emotion regulation

– Interpersonal Effectiveness

Research Backed Efficacy

DBT is known to reduce suicidal ideations and reduce high hospitalization rates, as noted in the Archhives of General Psychiatry Journal. Compared to standard therapy, it has high efficacy rates in treatment of personality disorders. Chronic emotional dysregulation and self harming behaviors see a positive turnaround in many difficult cases, as represented by the findings in The American Journal of Psychiatry.

Skills that Help in Everyday Life

One of the best features about DBT is its practicality. It serves as a great tool to handle situations that are not just hypothetical but are present in an everyday lifestyle of the individual. It acts as a way out for people to reduce their impulsive urges and find a solution to their dysregulation in real time. At mental health centers across the city run by some of the experienced psychologist in Gurugram, DBT has been integrated as an integral part of most treatment plans.

DBT serves people more than a therapy- it’s a toolkit that helps them navigate their lives in a more structured and present manner. With the support from a right psychiatrist and dedicated team of experts, it’s a smooth road ahead.

title: How does Environment Affect Mental Health?
h1: The Impact of Environment on Mental Health
excerpt: The Impact of Environment on Mental Health Our life is made up of a variety of experiences- good and bad. Every experience that we have affects us in some way or the other, building our perception and mindset along the way. Keeping this fact in mind, our mental health is also a product of our […]
contentHtml:
Our life is made up of a variety of experiences- good and bad. Every experience that we have affects us in some way or the other, building our perception and mindset along the way. Keeping this fact in mind, our mental health is also a product of our interactions with the environment. As a mental hospital in Gurgaon, people often approach our psychiatrist with questions about their emotions and inner turmoils. But it is very seldom that they stop to take a look at their immediate environment. It is this particular reason that many of us have an onset of a variety of mental health conditions. 

Today, let’s analyze how our environment affects us in particular ways that shape our psyche and positive mindset.

The Impact of Urban Lifestyle

Migration from a slow and mindful lifestyle to a sedentary urban one has had a major impact on the mental health of people. According to the landmark study published in Nature Journal, people who reside in urban areas have a higher chance of developing issues like depression, anxiety and schizophrenia compared to their rural counterparts. 

The overstimulation and social stress from our everyday interactions increase the activity in Amygdala that result in these stress responses.

Toxic Work & Home Environment

Beyond our mind, our surroundings play an equally important role in maintaining an equilibrium in our lives. A chaotic household has many issues that people fail to identify, that are harmful in the long term. Chronic anxiety and low resilience in adulthood can be some major issues to encounter as time passes. 

Toxic work culture, unsupportive peers and relationships are also a crucial part of developing mental health conditions. As a top mental hospital in Gurgaon, our team of psychiatrist truly suggest individuals to analyze their environment whenever they approach us with their issues. This way, they are able to identify their triggers, what surrounds them and how these environmental factors affect them.

contentHtml:
Exploring Alcoholism in Families

When it comes to habits that destroy and put negative things in the mind, alcoholism usually takes the first spot. It is a dreadful act sold as tradition in many aspects, that has trickled its way down into the sedentary lifestyle. Now, in today’s society, alcohol consumption is seen as a recreational activity, means to indulge in society or simply as a status symbol. But what goes on behind this habit is something we all need to understand. As a mental hospital in Gurgaon, we see a variety of cases that stem solely from alcoholism, and create issues that take years to resolve. 

Coming to the curious question of the day, is it really the case that alcoholism can run in families? The answer is Yes- but not in the way it may seem. With genetics and environmental conditions playing a significant role- it is easier to explain why this can happen.

Genetic Conditions

Alcohol Use Disorder can account for 50% of the cases that are backed by genetic predisposition, as accounted by JAMA psychiatry. Children whose parents have previously suffered are 4-10 times likely to develop the disorder as well. This explains the high percentage of passing on a habit rather than it being just a tradition. As per our conversations with our psychiatrist in Gurgaon, many people often display a family history of alcoholism when they show up with mental health and related issues. 

Environmental Factors

Parenting styles, family conflicts, peer groups and exposure to alcohol during childhood leave a lasting impact on the psyche of an individual. This is bound to increase the risk of an individual developing alcoholism, regardless of their genetic composition. As a mental hospital in Gurgaon, we witness that this is a cycle that runs through generations and has a notorious habit of continuation. Providing early intervention and therapy can help. When you consult with some of the best psychiatrists in Gurgaon, you find the right kind of guidance and therapies through years of expertise and understanding. 

Treatment plans often consist of family therapies and individual counselling sessions that are coupled with detoxification and rehabilitation activities. Alcoholism can run in families- but that does not have to stop you in pursuing what is right for you and your future. If you see your loved ones suffering from this issue- it is time to step up and take a positive direction towards recovery.

title: What Causes Cluster A Personality Disorder?

excerpt: Understanding the Causes of Cluster A Personality Disorders When people talk about personality disorders, it is often seen with a mix of complexity and undealt issues. contentHtml:
When people talk about personality disorders, it is often seen with a mix of complexity and undealt issues. Personality issues are often seen as simple acts of dissociating from one’s usual characteristics and acting out of the blue. But beware, that is not the case. When you take an in depth approach, you realize about the many aspects and complex ideas. Similar is the case with Cluster A disorders, that include Paranoid, Schizoid and Schizotypal personality disorders. 

So, dwelling upon the fact that their origin has a root, let’s talk about the causes that lead to its onset and rapid development.

1. Genetic Predisposition

A large portion of personality comes from genetic factors. People who have a family history of mental illnesses like schizophrenia or related disorders have a higher chance of developing Cluster A disorders. This is because of the irregularities that show up in dopamine regulation that influence reality and forming social connections.

A study in the American Journal of Psychiatry revealed that people who have first degree relatives suffering from Schizotypal PD have a high chance of developing it themselves. With the help of a qualified psychiatrist in Gurgaon, one can confirm root causes and approach treatment appropriately.

2. Early Development Patterns

Our early development and experiences have a major impact on our personality traits. When people grow up in neglected and negative environments, it affects them accordingly. They may have issues with trust, social safety and emotional regulation. Such problems may lead to disorders developing in the ballpark of Cluster A. If you visit a mental hospital in Gurgaon, the diagnosis can reveal a whole lot just from the childhood history itself.

3. Social Isolation and Cultural Influences

If an individual faces social alienation for a long time, it can push them towards isolation. This can serve as a prerequisite for the onset of Cluster A disorders. In spaces of high stress and demands, a person may even develop paranoia to shield themselves from the consequences. 

From the perspective of a top psychiatrist in Gurgaon, these factors can combine in any ratio and amplify the level of issues, leading to development and onset of a disorder.

Although complex, Cluster A disorders are not untreatable. With just the right amount of insight and help, management and control of Personality Disorders is possible. With early intervention and treatment plans, people can turn their lives around. title: What is Deep TMS Therapy?
h1: Deep TMS Therapy: What You Need to Know
excerpt: Deep TMS Therapy: What You Need to Know Mental health treatment has come a long way. In our pursuit of finding the best mental health resources, we have made many innovations. One of the most appraised and widely recognized innovations in mental health today is deep Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Therapy (dTMS), which has taken the […]
contentHtml:
Mental health treatment has come a long way. In our pursuit of finding the best mental health resources, we have made many innovations. One of the most appraised and widely recognized innovations in mental health today is deep Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Therapy (dTMS), which has taken the industry by storm. If you’re hearing about this for the first time, don’t worry- we’ll break it down for you. 

As a rehabilitation center, we take it on ourselves to enlighten the community on the recent advancements in the field. With a team of some of the best psychologist in delhi and across India, let’s explore what dTMS helps with.

What Exactly is dTMS?

dTMS is a non-invasive brain stimulation technique that targets certain areas of the brain using magnetic waves. It targets specific areas of the brain associated with mental health conditions like depression, OCD, and anxiety. Unlike traditional TMS that only penetrates the surface, dTMS actually reaches deep areas of the brain that makes it more effective in nature. 

Here, a special helmet with magnetic coils is placed on the person’s head, where magnetic pulses stimulate less-active neural pathways. 

Does this Process Hurt?

Contrary to the popular belief- not at all! This process is perfectly safe. It is felt as a tingling sensation on your scalp and a person can return to their daily activities right after a session.  Sessions usually last for 20 minutes, with the frequency decided by a healthcare expert in a rehabilitation center.

Studies have shown that dTMS can be life changing, especially for people who don’t respond well to traditional treatment plans. According to a study in the Journal of Psychiatric Research, people with treatment resistant depression respond well to this therapy. Another study published in Brain Stimulation pointed towards its efficacy in managing symptoms of OCD. 

If you are considering treatment with dTMS, consulting with a top psychiatrist in India is essential. This gives you an edge to understand what is right for you in the long run. 

Remember- mental health journey today is not just about surviving- it’s also about being the best version of yourself. Approach Tulasi Healthcare today and let us help you empower your journey to wellness.

As home to some best psychiatrist in Delhi, let’s break down some of the points This will help you assess & ensure if your child needs psychiatric support.

1. Persistent Changes in Mood and Behavior

Kids can be moody! It’s a part of their growth spurt, a truly natural process. It can come and go in waves, and that’s totally okay! But the fact to consider here is- if they stay withdrawn, sad and anxious for weeks- its a sign to approach an expert. According to The Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, chronic emotional distress in children often goes unrecognized and untreated, despite early symptoms being present.

2. Sudden Decline in Academic Performance

This is a very clear sign of impact on mental health. It is a sign worth paying attention to. When the child starts shifting their focus from the things they usually do, it is because some other factor is taking a toll on them. Difficulty concentrating or remembering things can be tied to anxiety, depression, or attention disorders.

3. Trouble with Sleep and Appetite

Sleeping too much or too little is a sign that can be casted into the risky bucket. The Pediatrics journal focuses on the importance of early intervention to improve the level of anxiety and mental health that could later affect chronic conditions in adulthood.

Every child is different- and if your child seeks help does not mean that you have failed as a parent. title: What is MECT?
h1: Understanding MECT: A Comprehensive Overview
excerpt: Understanding MECT: A Comprehensive Overview When people search and talk about Electroconvulsive Therapy, their usual reaction is to think about the harsh and outdated methods. But today, times have changed and so has our approach towards mental well being. Today’s reality is quite different. It is totally opposite of the scenes portrayed in old movies […]
contentHtml:
When people search and talk about Electroconvulsive Therapy, their usual reaction is to think about the harsh and outdated methods. But today, times have changed and so has our approach towards mental well being. Today’s reality is quite different. It is totally opposite of the scenes portrayed in old movies and previously documented methods. With new modifications, Electroconvulsive Therapy has turned into a sought after non-traditional therapy for many conditions. 

mECT is a safe, refined and controlled method of amplifying treatment for those who are not able to receive results from traditional treatment. It’s not as scary as it sounds- and for many, it can be a life altering decision.

What is MECT?

mECT exactly is a non-traditional therapy that stimulates different parts of the brain through a brief and controlled current. It passes through the specific region and resets the brain chemistry to provide relief from different conditions. These disorders usually include- bipolar disorder, major depression & schizophrenia, as per some of the best psychiatrist in India. The modification here is that the individual is given muscle relaxants and put under general anesthesia so that they are devoid of any pain. Such ethical consideration observed under previous engagement makes it modified today.

A good psychiatrist in India will move towards mECT in cases where traditional therapies like Medication and Talk therapy are not able to provide relief. 

What does the Procedure Involve?

– Pre-Procedure– The client undergoes in-depth evaluation and fasting before the procedure starts.

– Under Supervision– The patient is given anesthesia and a muscle relaxant. Electrodes are placed on the scalp, and a brief electrical impulse is delivered. The entire procedure lasts just a few minutes.

– Post-Procedure–  Patients usually wake up within 10–15 minutes and are monitored for a short time before being discharged or returned to their room.

Clients  usually report feeling well adjusted and better during 6-12 weeks of their treatment sessions.

Is it a Safe Procedure?

Yes. mECT is a very safe procedure as it is provided under controlled conditions, like a rehabilitation centre. According to a study in The Lancet Psychiatry, mECT continues to be one of the most effective treatment modalities for severe depression. It is easier to apply in many conditions and is extremely comfortable due to the use of muscle relaxants and anesthesia (Indian Journal of Psychiatry).

While mECT has always been under the lens, it has proven to be effective and humane for many. As a rehabilitation center, we advocate for more options like mECT for clients suffering from severe conditions.

title: What Foods Help with Depression?

excerpt: Can Food Help with Depression? Whenever we hear about depression, the first thought that pops up in our minds is that it can be managed easily. Usually we go with some therapy & medications, and that is what our knowledge is limited to most of the time. But the answer to our issues also lies […]
contentHtml:
Whenever we hear about depression, the first thought that pops up in our minds is that it can be managed easily. Usually we go with some therapy & medications, and that is what our knowledge is limited to most of the time. But the answer to our issues also lies in small factors that contribute daily to its development and onset. 

What we eat definitely plays a role in how we feel. But no single food source is responsible for ‘curing’ the symptoms of depression. A balanced and nourishing diet supports heightened brain function, mood regulation and emotional wellbeing. Now, many clinics run by psychiatrist in Delhi along with programs run by rehabilitation center have also integrated this approach.

The Mood & Food Algorithm

There is an old saying that goes- ‘we are what we eat’. This holds true to some extent, given our nutritional habits affect our lifestyle and hence our mental health. Our brain needs a good supply of nutrients to function at its optimal level. When deficiencies arise, so do health issues. Deficiencies in certain vitamins, minerals, and fatty acids can contribute to feelings of low energy, irritability, and sadness.

A study published in BMC Medicine discovered a great diet plan.People who adopted a Mediterranean style diet rich in vegetables, legumes, whole grains, fruits, nuts, and healthy fat experienced reduction in depressive symptoms. This raised a stark difference from western diet and lifestyle.

So, What are the Best Foods to Include in your Diet to Help with Depression?

– Leafy Green Vegetables: Spinach, Kale and Broccoli are foods that are rich in Vitamin B and folate. Low folate is usually associated with higher rates of depression.

– Omega 3 Rich Foods: Oats, brown rice, and quinoa are a good source of serotonin production. They provide a great energy boost to the body. 

– Fermented Foods: Yogurt, kefir, and kimchi improve gut health. Mind and gut health are strongly interconnected, so eating these supports a balanced mood.

– Nuts and Seeds: Almonds, walnuts, and flaxseeds are rich in magnesium, selenium and healthy fats that ease anxiety and depressive symptoms.

 

Some of the best psychiatrist in Delhi clinics and top rehabilitation centre programs now include nutritionally impactful diets along with therapy and medication. A recent review in The Lancet Psychiatry emphasized that nutritional psychiatry is a growing field with robust evidence linking diet to mental health outcomes.

title: Are Mood Swings Always a Sign of Bipolar Disorder?
h1: Is Every Mood Swing a Sign of Bipolar Disorder?
excerpt: Is Every Mood Swing a Sign of Bipolar Disorder? There are times when we suddenly feel irritable and then return to our happy self the very next moment. This can happen to any of us, given the circumstances, and it’s only natural. But if it happens very frequently without any reason to facilitate it, one […]
contentHtml:
There are times when we suddenly feel irritable and then return to our happy self the very next moment. This can happen to any of us, given the circumstances, and it’s only natural. But if it happens very frequently without any reason to facilitate it, one might wonder. ‘Am I suffering from a mood disorder?’ Well, the answer here may be yes. But not all mood swings mean that you might be suffering from Bipolar Disorder. 

Mood changes are a part of being human. Daily stressors, work demands, relationship issues and lack of sleep can become a reason for any mood issue. That does not mean it is simply bipolar behavior. These shifts are usually short-lived and tied to specific triggers. In bipolar disorder, though, mood changes are more intense, long-lasting, and often disconnected from outside events.

Bipolar disorder is a clinical condition that involves episodes of mania, hypomania and depression. These episodes can last for days, weeks or even months, without any reason and ways of improvement. According to The American Journal of Psychiatry, more than 2.4% of the world population suffers from Bipolar disorder, but quite a lot of these people go undiagnosed. This is due to the fact that these people suffer from mood problems but fail to meet the proper criteria.

So, what might cause the mood swings if not bipolar disorder?

● Stress and Anxiety

● Hormonal changes (especially during PMS, pregnancy, or menopause)

● Sleep disturbances

● Personality traits or disorders

● Substance use or withdrawal

● Chronic medical conditions like thyroid imbalances

 

It is also worth noting that people also often misdiagnose themselves based upon the information that is available online. WIthout any expert intervention, it should not be considered a formal diagnosis of any sort. If you are a resident of Delhi, consulting a psychiatrist in Delhi is the smartest step one can take. If the condition requires intensive support, a rehabilitation centre specialized in mental health may provide a structured environment for treatment and recovery.

Another study in The Lancet Psychiatry also pointed towards the importance of keen and expert intervention. Most times, bipolar disorder is interpreted as anxiety, depression or even ADHD without proper context. This type of misdiagnosis can affect the treatment plan by years. 

So, mood swings can definitely indicate a sign of mental illness, but not necessarily bipolar disorder. Whether it is stress, trauma, or something truly critical, it is not necessary for you to face it alone. The best psychiatrist in Delhi can help decode the patterns and guide you towards healing.

title: Mental Health Stigma in India
h1: How Tulasi Healthcare is Breaking Mental Health Stigma in India
excerpt: How Tulasi Healthcare is Breaking Mental Health Stigma in India For decades, mental health has garnered stigma in every way possible. From its approach to treatment plans, the Indian subcontinent has taken its time to accept this field. People believed that anyone approaching a psychiatrist must be someone unstable, and not considered a part of […]
contentHtml:
For decades, mental health has garnered stigma in every way possible. From its approach to treatment plans, the Indian subcontinent has taken its time to accept this field. People believed that anyone approaching a psychiatrist must be someone unstable, and not considered a part of society anymore. No matter how well they do, that tag could not leave them for their lifetime. Families hid diagnoses, students suffered in silence, and professionals wore masks of strength while quietly falling apart inside. But slowly and surely, things are changing.

So, what is the scene behind this shift? How is the landscape changing for the better?

The Old Mindset: What will People Say?

Let’s all face it- the Indian society places more importance on the level of appearances rather on their mental health. Admitting to having any mental health concerns like anxiety, depression and personality issues is considered a weakness. But the truth seems to trump the fact- 1 in 7 Indians face mental health issues, as per The Lancet Psychiatry. This is in no way a small number- it encompasses millions of people. 

The Turning Point: Conversations, Celebrities and COVID

A major shift started happening when the media took over this campaign. With the support of psychiatrists in India during Covid times, the conversation escalated. Many celebrities like Deepika Padukone talked about their journey with depression, which normalized the conversation around these topics. Suddenly burnout and depression were things everyone could relate to. 

The Role of Awareness

Social media and online ongoing campaigns have added a plethora of awareness regarding mental health. Now, it is easier to read about symptoms, assess oneself and approach any psychiatrist in India. People these days are starting to see that now approaching mental health is not a last resort- it is an opportunity towards wellbeing. According to Indian Journal Of Psychiatry, Urban India has seen a 35% rise in people seeking voluntary treatment.

What can You Do?

Talk, Share & Ask questions. Whether it’s supporting a friend, seeking help yourself, or encouraging a loved one to see an expert, every small action takes away the stigma.

We’re still a work in progress, but the silence is finally being replaced with strength & stories. And that’s how real change begins—with one honest conversation at a time.

title: Can Depression be Genetic?
h1: Exploring the Genetic Basis of Depression
excerpt: Exploring the Genetic Basis of Depression Do you ever wonder why some people who have depression usually have a family history of the same? Why do the symptoms tend to run in families despite changing circumstances for all? Well, the question is a genuine one and requires a keen eye. At Tulasi Healthcare, we come […]
contentHtml:
Do you ever wonder why some people who have depression usually have a family history of the same? Why do the symptoms tend to run in families despite changing circumstances for all? Well, the question is a genuine one and requires a keen eye. At Tulasi Healthcare, we come across many clients that ask us similar questions on a daily basis.

With this blog, we aim to answer all the questions of genetics that link to depression. Let’s take a look at how genetics have an impact on depression.

Yes, Depression can be Genetic. But it does not Answer all the Questions.

Genetics do have a part to play in depression, but it does not quite exactly display the full picture. According to a study published in Nature Genetics, scientists have duly identified some genes that link to depression, but not necessarily “cause” it. This means that our environment, its stress, trauma and triggering events also have a role to play.

So, genetics do have a role to play, but it does not necessarily trigger its onset.

What if Depression Runs in my Family?

As discussed above, it generally has other factors adding to its onset. This simply means that you have to be more proactive and aware about your environment, stressors and handle them with insight. Recognizing early signs is essential and psychoeducation helps. Some of the best psychiatrist in Gurgaon often recommend regular checkups for those with family history.

Is there a Test to Identify Depression Genes?

There are some highly advanced tests that can be done to identify the ‘possibility’ of depression through genetics. Identification of such genes is yet a long road in scientific journey. If you are concerned, speaking to a psychiatrist in Gurgaon can be a good way to plan ahead. According to the American Journal of Psychiatry, mental health professionals combine family history, genetic predispositions and lifestyle to create more personalized treatments.

The Good News? Depression is Treatable.

Whether you have a genetic predisposition or just affected through environmental factors- help is available. Therapy, lifestyle changes, and in some cases, medication can make a big difference. And remember, reaching out for help isn’t a sign of weakness—it’s a step toward strength.

So yes, depression can be genetic. But more importantly, it can be faced—and managed—with the right support.

h1: A Guide to the Most Common Psychiatric Tests
excerpt: A Guide to the Most Common Psychiatric Tests When you think about a psychiatric test, it might spring up dramatic scenes that one imagines in a lab-clipboards, cards and inkblots spread from here to there. But if you have stumbled upon our blog today to know about some common psychiatric tests- then you are at […]
contentHtml:
When you think about a psychiatric test, it might spring up dramatic scenes that one imagines in a lab-clipboards, cards and inkblots spread from here to there. But if you have stumbled upon our blog today to know about some common psychiatric tests- then you are at the right place!

Considering your options amongst good psychiatric experts is essential, especially when it comes to choosing a psychiatrist in India. Dr. Gorav Gupta shares his insights on the topic to raise awareness towards mental health amongst his readers. 

1. The Mental Status Examination (MSE)

This test acts as a general setup of psychiatry. Here, an overall examination of the client’s physical, emotional and psychological condition is done. They might ask you simple questions to assess your memory, mood, and orientation (like knowing the date or where you are). 

With its help, some pain points are considered and sorted that help in reaching towards a diagnosis. 

2. Beck Depression Inventory (BDI)

This is a very widely used self reporting test to shell out the symptoms of depression and any associated disorders. It is clinically validated in multiple studies and can be a great way to assess other related issues. (Journal of Clinical Psychology)

3. Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A)

This test is a classic to measure the symptoms of anxiety with any possible insights. A psychiatrist in India can help you manage these with ease. According to the American Journal of Psychiatry, it is still one of the most effective ways to measure anxiety and its effective symptoms.

4. Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory

This test dwells into deeper personality traits and psychological conditions. It’s often used when a psychiatrist needs a broad overview of a person’s mental health landscape. It can help diagnose everything from mood disorders to personality disorders. And no—it’s not a “pass or fail” test!

5. Cognitive and Neuropsychological Tests

These tests assess your brain for any neurological abnormalities. You might be asked to solve some simple tasks and questions so that the experts can understand your brain functioning and any loopholes that exist.

Do remember that these tests are not about putting you in a spectrum. They are about assessing your conditio to push yourself in the positive direction of healing. Your mind deserves just as much attention as your body—so don’t hesitate to take that first step toward understanding it better.

contentHtml:
If you have ever sat across a psychiatrist during a diagnosis, you must have definitely wondered one thing- how do they know to ask the right question? Well, it is the insight of an expert that guides them in the right direction. The process of diagnosis may seem very mysterious, but it is quite structured and thoughtful. It is designed in a way that a person unfolds their issues with least effort. Think of it like the work of a detective- but it works for your mind!

Let’s look at the six essential questions psychiatrist in Delhi often start with during their sessions:

1. What Symptoms are You Experiencing?

This is a question that lays the foundation of an investigative process. Apart from what the body expresses, having an idea of a person’s emotional state is essential to move ahead. Identifying these points helps in narrowing the diagnosis. Duration and severity matter too. Are these feelings new or long-standing? Mild or completely disruptive?

2. When did the Symptoms Start?

Timing is everything when it comes to diagnosis. If the issue is diagnosed early, the management and results can be miraculous. If there is delay in understanding what happens, unknown complications may occur.

3. How do these Problems Affect Your Daily Life?

If the person is not able to carry on with their daily life due to their issues, their problems have taken over. A study in Psychiatric Services indicated that Functional Impairment is directly related to mental illness severity.

4. Do you have a family history of mental health issues?

Mental health, like any other aspect of our lives, is inherited through our genetic ties. A study published in JAMA Psychiatry revealed that many psychiatric conditions have tremendous genetic ties.

5. Have you Ever had Thoughts of Self Harm?

This is a question that helps us gauge the severity of the disorder. As a team of renowned psychiatrist in Delhi, Tulasi Health Care takes extreme measures to safeguard the clients in such cases.

6. What is Going on in Your Life Right Now?

Current conditions usually have a strong impact on the person’s mental health in a variety of ways. Understanding these factors can help experts to find the right set of treatments and interventions. 

Diagnosis isn’t about labels; it’s about understanding your story and finding a path forward. Follow Tulasi Healthcare for more mental health updates!

title: Burnout vs Depression: What’s the Difference?
h1: Burnout or Depression? Key Differences You Should Know
excerpt: Burnout or Depression? Key Differences You Should Know It’s easy to feel drained in the sedentary lifestyle that has been built today. People continue with their lives in one way or the other, but sometimes fail to understand if it’s just burnout they are facing or slipping into depression. But what they fail to understand […]
contentHtml:
It’s easy to feel drained in the sedentary lifestyle that has been built today. People continue with their lives in one way or the other, but sometimes fail to understand if it’s just burnout they are facing or slipping into depression. But what they fail to understand is that intervention is necessary in such cases. Let’s see how we can be of help.

The look of these two can be remarkably similar on the surface, displaying classic signs and fitting into categories. But the true answer lies within the innermost dwelling and diagnosis. There are important differences that a professional—like a psychiatrist in India—can help you recognize.

Burnout is typically related to work induced stress. It is more situational in nature with regards to depression. As the situation changes and leaves room for improvement, the symptoms of burnout dissipate gradually. It’s often reversible with rest, boundary-setting, or changes in your environment.

Depression on the other hand, is more clinical than situational in nature. No matter the situation or environment, the problems are more intrinsically driven. People with depression experience:

– Persistent Sadness or Loneliness

– Loss of interest in tasks that were once enjoyed

– Sleep Issues 

– Appetite Changes

– Feelings of Worthlessness and Invalidation

– Thoughts of Self Harm 

According to a study in the World Psychiatry Journal, burnout is a stepping stone towards depression if not given proper and early intervention. Many cases of burnout also turnout to be cases of depression, on account of misdiagnosis. (Journal of Affective Disorders)

This is why it is important not to self diagnose and deflate the sense of what you are feeling. Minimizing what you feel may lead to severe problems, especially reducing the efficacy of your overall life. You can talk to a psychiatrist in India and resolve all your concerns, especially when it comes to topics like these. It is truly important to know that your mental health comes before anything else, since it has a significant impact on every other aspect of your life. 

Whether it’s burnout or depression, it is important to know that both are treatment and manageable in the long term. Approach Tulasi Healthcare to explore what it means to be in the best of your health today.
