h1: blood tests indicating risk of future mental illness
excerpt: We’ll be honest- if we told anyone a few years ago that a blood test would reveal their risk of developing a mental health disorder- they’d probably not believe us. It is a topic of sheer inquisitivity and concern, that many still have questions in their mind regarding this. Mental illness has always been a […]
contentHtml:
We’ll be honest- if we told anyone a few years ago that a blood test would reveal their risk of developing a mental health disorder- they’d probably not believe us. It is a topic of sheer inquisitivity and concern, that many still have questions in their mind regarding this. Mental illness has always been a deeply intangible and critical part of all our lives. It has always been a deeply personal topic for all. Thinking that a mental health disorder can now show up during a simple blood screening- is a fact that we are still wrapping our heads around!

Now, researchers have moved a step ahead with a significant step into the mental health space. Introducing blood tests that can signify the probability of developing a mental disorder. This is even before onset and symptoms- a huge leap indeed! As a team passionate about growing the space of mental health, Tulasi Health Care is here with its insights to tell its audience about new advancements.

The Science behind Detecting disorders

So how can a vial of blood reveal what is going on in our minds? As it turns out, a lot more than we thought!

Our blood is home to many things, but our concern today is with biomarkers. They constitute specific proteins, hormones and genetic materials. Now why may these be important? Since our cognitive functions and mood are regulated by them in some way or the other, it is a definitive path to a good diagnosis.

Taking an example- Some proteins like interleukin-6 (IL-6) and C-reactive protein (CRP), both are  linked to inflammation. These have been found at higher levels in people who later developed depression or schizophrenia. These markers don’t “prove” a person will get a mental illness, but they can suggest a higher vulnerability.

Advances in genomics today can also determine certain genetic mutations that can indicate a higher vulnerability of developing ADHD or bipolar disorder. The research is still ongoing, but definitely holds great potential.

How do these tests work?

When one usually imagines a blood test, they think of a chilly, cold clinic with people rushing in and out. The interesting part is what happens next.

Once your blood sample is collected, it is scanned for some particular biomarkers that are related to specific disorders. Some tests take over inflammatory markers, while some focus on genetic and metabolic patterns. The result is a risk profile- it’s basically a personalized insight into the likelihood of developing certain conditions.

These tests can have a significant impact on the speed and efficacy of providing a diagnosis, especially in cases where there are many facets to consider. It can be a great option to apply in an organizational setting, providing a deep insight and help to many clients. Our EAP program, Thriving Minds is a perfect space to discover the efficacy of such tests. Since individuals are always looking for the right answer for their issues while managing their career, it can definitely prove to be a great tool.

This test is more like a rain check- it will show us the probability of having a disorder in our lifetimes.

List of specific blood tests

As identified, some specific blood tests can help in identifying probable disorders. Let’s take a look at different types-

Test

What It Detects

Linked Mental Health Risk if Deficient

Vitamin B12

Neurotransmitter synthesis, myelin health

Depression, memory loss, irritability, psychosis

Folate (Vitamin B9)

Methylation, brain development

Depression, cognitive decline, prenatal risk of schizophrenia

Vitamin D (25-OH D)

Neuroprotection, serotonin synthesis

Depression, schizophrenia, seasonal affective disorder (SAD)

Iron Studies (Ferritin, Iron, TIBC)

Oxygen transport to brain, dopamine production

ADHD, fatigue, anxiety, developmental delays

Magnesium

NMDA receptor modulation, stress regulation

Anxiety, depression, sleep disturbances, migraines

Zinc

Neurogenesis, modulating glutamate/GABA

Depression, mood swings, cognitive impairment

Homocysteine

Marker of B12/folate deficiency & methylation dysfunction

High levels associated with depression, dementia risk

Omega-3 Index (EPA + DHA)

Anti-inflammatory, synaptic function

Depression, ADHD, bipolar disorder

Thyroid Panel (TSH, Free T3, Free T4)

Metabolism regulation, mood, energy

Hypothyroidism: depression, fatigue; Hyperthyroidism: anxiety, restlessness

Blood Glucose / HbA1c

Brain glucose utilization

Cognitive decline, anxiety, mood swings in insulin resistance

Utility in Mental Health transformation

Let’s talk about practical implications- how does it matter?

An early detection is directly linked to an early support, leading to higher recovery and wellbeing rates. For mental health professionals, this is a game changer. We’ve long relied on interviews and behavioral observations—subjective tools—to diagnose complex conditions. Objective data from blood tests can supplement those tools and help reduce misdiagnosis, which is still alarmingly common.

This test will not exactly be crystal balls of destiny. But it will definitely allow us to proceed in the right direction and find the correct answers in a short time.

Ready to take charge of your mental health?

Mental health today is on the brink of a breakthrough scientific revolution. Whether it’s through medical advancements like these or deeper conversations, the future is about understanding the mind more clearly than ever before.

Let’s change how we think about mental health—starting now with Tulasi Healthcare.

It is a very real, astonishing condition that affects how we think, feel and behave in our true environment. But the only fact that […]
contentHtml:
Let’s be honest- coping with depression isn’t as simple as ‘being positive’. It is also about many different aspects that surround its being. It is a very real, astonishing condition that affects how we think, feel and behave in our true environment. But the only fact that matters is- when you get the right direction and care- it’s manageable to an extent.

So, the word here to focus on is being ‘effective’. Being effective in your methods to cope with depression requires expert guidance and tons of research to see what works well for you. Well, with your lucky stars- you’ve found Tulasi Healthcare’s blog!

Acknowledge How You are Feeling

First things first- pay attention to how you are feeling. It is the very crux of feeling things that leads you to your diagnosis. The more we validate our emotions instead of fighting them, the easier it becomes to respond with care.

Building a Routine

Believe it or not, but having a routine actually helps. Starting small is the key- getting out of bed and just taking showers can do wonders. These actions send signals to your brain that you are in control, even when things feel heavy.

Move Around and Find Out!

Exercise and movement have a benefit that most things do not. They are proven mood boosters with the power to rewire your entire systems. With some light reading in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, we found that even a light stretch can release endorphins that can make or break your entire system! So, better take that extra lap if you can!

Talk Therapy

While CBT & DBT are good ways of catharsis, professional guidance can help you detangle your thoughts in a much better way. If you approach an expert and look for a good psychiatrist in India, they can help you determine the right tools and direction. 

Medicinal Management

Contrary to popular belief, it is not an issue to consume medications. Rather, they are a way to support your ongoing wellbeing through therapy. We must consider them as tools to control and reset our brain functions more clearly. (Journal of Clinical Psychiatry)

Don’t Underestimate Connection

Last but not the least, surround yourself with peers that uplift you, are positive and think in your regard.

If you are struggling and reading this blog, it’s a cue to approach a psychiatrist in India and get all the help you need. Remember, it’s all about taking that first step!

contentHtml:
What to Expect from the Environment of a Rehabilitation Center

While hearing the words ‘rehabilitation center’, the minds of most people dart towards an ugly isolated space. This mindset is prevalent in many cultures and societies. Its also quite normal to see people taking a step away at the mention of its name, stigmatizing its existence even more. But the situation is quite the opposite. With such major advancements in the mental health field, the perception towards the purpose and existence of a rehabilitation center have taken a positive turn.

The environment inside a modern rehab facility is something to look for in a positive space. Hope, support and warmth line every nook and corner, despite what the stereotypes might dictate. It’s designed to promote healing, comfort, and emotional safety.

So, what can you truly expect from the environment of a rehabilitation center?

A Safe and Supportive Environment

These points define the true pillars on which a rehabilitation center stands. Its a structured yet compassionate space of healing and support. When a person is suffering from addiction, substance abuse, or difficult mental health concerns, they are bound to lash out. They go through many behavioral changes that require patience and compassion to deal with. This setting plays a key role in maintaining a grounded reality for them.

Emotional Safety and Flexibility

The power of emotional safety is exceptional. It is one of the most crucial identifications of a safe environment. Healing as a process requires immense emotional support and flexibility in ideas of the caregivers. This means providing spaces free from stigma, where individuals can explore their traumas, rebuild self-esteem, and learn healthier coping mechanisms.

Calm and Comfortable Spaces

A rehab center is intentionally designed to be a calm and collected space for these reasons-
● Quiet resting areas with little to no disturbances
● Common rooms for group therapy, activities, or simply unwinding
● Outdoor spaces like gardens for internal reflection and fresh air

A therapeutic environment where such elements are embedded add to the long term recovery of an individual, according to The Lancet Psychiatry. Plus, having individualized care plans add to a person’s ability to reintegrate into everyday life after treatment, according to Indian Journal of Psychiatry.

A rehabilitation center is not a place of restriction, its a place of renewal. The environment is designed to make you feel supported, not punished. And for many, it becomes the first place where true healing begins.

title: Do rehabilitation center cure addiction?
h1: Do rehabilitation center cure addiction?
excerpt: Can rehabilitation centers help overcome addiction? contentHtml:
Can rehabilitation centers help overcome addiction?

When an individual suffers from addiction, the question that majorly runs through their mind is one- can a rehabilitation center cure addiction? It is a fair question, given families and individuals invest their finance, time and effort into it. Their hopes and dreams of a better life are tied to this question.

The short answer? A rehabilitation centre doesn’t offer a magic cure. But it can absolutely put someone on the path to long-term recovery.

Addiction is not an issue that has a quick fix.

It is similar to any other issue like hypertension and diabetes- but it takes more than willpower here to get it under control. It affects the brain’s reward system that hampers its ability to chase goals and live a positive life. Curing addiction is not just related to mere medical interventions- it is also about the positive long term aspects that come with it. Rehab centers come with a structured and supportive environment that aids in resolving emotional, psychological and behavioral patterns.

Let’s see what typically happens in a rehab setting-

  • Detoxification– Here, all the symptoms are managed in a safe and supervised environment.
  • Therapeutic intervention– After stabilization from detoxification sets in, therapies like CBT, REBT are introduced for the clients to reimagine their thinking patterns.
  • Psychiatric care– Many individuals suffer from conditions like anxiety, depression and other disorders that are managed simultaneously through medications.
  • Life skills training– This is a very crucial part of recovery that defines many aspects of long term management. Rehab programs often include help with stress management, relapse prevention, communication, and goal setting.
  • Aftercare planning– The road to recovery does not stop when a person leaves the facility. It is a long journey, where every milestone matters.

So, do all of these things manage to cure addiction? Not quite exactly. These things ‘manage’ the symptoms well and set a person on the path to recovery. As per The Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA), relapse rates for addiction are similar to any other chronic condition. These hover at around 50-60%, marking a significant number.

A rehabilitation center’s main aim is to provide a portal of better support, tools and hope for a better life. Success depends on many factors, including the individual’s willingness to change, the quality of the program, and the strength of their support system after discharge.

A holistic, person centered approach is the most effective when it comes to rehabilitation, as stated by The Indian Journal of Psychiatry.

Summing it up, with the right determination, care and support, management also feels like a cure.

title: Do rehabilitation centers take adolescents?
h1: Do Rehab Centers Accept Teenagers?
excerpt: Do Rehab Centers Accept Teenagers? Whenever we think of rehab, our first thought is of thoroughly exhausted adults going through a series of treatments. But is it true? But here’s a growing reality: more and more adolescents are also facing these issues. The numbers are going exponentially and people are confused. Do rehabilitation centers offer […]
contentHtml:
Whenever we think of rehab, our first thought is of thoroughly exhausted adults going through a series of treatments. But is it true? But here’s a growing reality: more and more adolescents are also facing these issues. The numbers are going exponentially and people are confused. Do rehabilitation centers offer help to adolescents too? Well, the answer is Yes.

Adolescence is a time of major physical, emotional and cognitive changes. Any wrong step can change an individual’s direction of life for the worse. Most mental health conditions manifest by the age of 14, according to the World Health Organization. This is an interesting number- given that most people seek help only when they are adults. They are mostly undiagnosed and untreated. Early intervention here plays a crucial role- approaching a rehabilitation center at the right time matters.

So, what exactly happens when an adolescent enters a rehabilitation centre?

It is important to be clear that these are not just some adult facilities where adolescents are kept without any facilities. Adolescent care programs are separate, where the treatment needs are tailored according to them.These programs do not only hold the sole purpose of removing addiction from their lives. They also help them understand their thought processes and critical concerns.

Upon entering the facility, a comprehensive assessment is provided to them in order to assess the issue. This includes evaluating their physical health, mental health, substance use history, academic performance, family dynamics, and emotional well-being.

The treatment plan often includes-

  • Individual therapy, focusing on their issues and underlying emotions
  • Group therapy to connect with peers facing similar challenges
  • Family therapy to assess dynamics and induce better recovery
  • Life skills training
  • Educational and occupational support

In some severe cases, medicinal management is essential to derive the best of the situational constraints.

According to The Journal of Adolescent Health, the adolescents that receive evidence based treatment show better recovery. With the help of family therapy combined with well researched treatment plans, better long term recovery was induced. The Indian Journal of Psychiatry  also highlights that early intervention in adolescent addiction leads to better outcomes and prevents long-term dependency.

One of the biggest advantages of these spaces is their focus on adolescent recovery. A safe and structured environment provides a space to heal, reflect and grow.

It is not just the involvement of addictive substances, but behavioral addictions as well that lead individuals to this space. If enrolled at the right time, rehabilitation center can become a boon for the adolescent  minds that crave care and concern.

contentHtml:
The word rehabilitation centre often brings up confused and mixed reactions from many. The name itself sounds strict, serious and full of regulations- but is that so?

Some people take it as a place of isolation and problems, but some see it as a place of restoring health and recovering. But a simple question remains- what happens behind the doors of a rehab centre?

Let’s take this mystery for a spin.

A rehabilitation centre is a place of recovery that is designed to facilitate treatment processes in a controlled environment. It helps people restore their strength from the issues of addiction, mental health disorders, or trauma from physical injuries. In the cases of mental health issues and addiction, these spaces provide a structured environment. This is essential because afflicted individuals can focus on getting better and solely interact with others for their betterment. Since it keeps them away from daily trials, tribulations and triggers of daily life, it is the perfect place for ensuring a fast paced recovery.

The first step

Assessment and history taking mark the first step of the rehabilitation journey. This process involves a comprehensive evaluation by psychologists, psychiatrists and a team of supportive psychiatric nurses and counselors. They look into the individual’s physical health, mental health, substance use history, and family background. On the basis of this information, a personalized treatment plan is put into place.

Second step

Detoxification marks the second step of the recovery journey. It is a medically supervised step to manage the triggers of withdrawal in cases of addiction. This process can last from a few days to a couple of weeks, depending on the severity of the case.  Detox is crucial but only the beginning; real recovery happens after this phase.

Once the detox phase has ended, the real work begins. Therapy is the focus at this stage which includes-

  • Individual Therapy- The clients connect individually with a therapist to resolve the root causes of their addiction and related mental health concerns.
  • Group Therapy- This helps people connect with clients that are facing similar challenges. This allows clients to raise their concerns effectively and learn from their surroundings too.
  • Family Therapy- Family Therapy plays a crucial role in rebuilding trust and communication in the family systems. This is essential to maintain a long term recovery. A popular study in The Indian Journal of Psychiatry shows when family therapy is involved in treatment plans, social integration is much higher.

Having a comprehensive treatment plan can be a great way to ensure long term recovery. As per a study published in The New England Journal of Medicine, structured treatment plays a significant role. When a holistic and structured treatment is coupled with therapeutic and medical interventions, there is an increased chance of  recovery success rates.

A rehabilitation centre like Tulasi healthcare is a second chance for many.  It’s a place where people can pause, heal, and rebuild their lives with the support of trained professionals and a nurturing environment.

title: Who is a psychiatrist? What does a psychiatrist do?
h1: Who is a psychiatrist?
excerpt: Mental health is finally getting all the attention that it deserves, and it is because of the professionals that maintain its integrity. With the recent advancements in the field of mental health, people are getting curious to know more about its aspects. One key figure in this field is a psychiatrist. Many individuals who seek […]
contentHtml:
Mental health is finally getting all the attention that it deserves, and it is because of the professionals that maintain its integrity. With the recent advancements in the field of mental health, people are getting curious to know more about its aspects. One key figure in this field is a psychiatrist. Many individuals who seek treatment tend to be confused between psychiatrists, psychologists and a counselor. With this in mind, let’s break down the role of a psychiatrist in a simple manner.

A psychiatrist is a medical professional who is trained in the basics and intricacies of mental health conditions. They are different from other practitioners since they can provide medical interventions to the clients in a trained, procedural manner. For example, someone is experiencing persistent anxiety and depression that is taking a toll on every aspect of their life. A psychiatrist here can do much more than a normal mental health practitioner. They can assess whether there’s a clinical diagnosis involved—like Generalized Anxiety Disorder or Major Depressive Disorder—and then decide if medication might help, alongside therapy.

What does a psychiatrist do?

One might wonder, what role does a psychiatrist have? How can they guide a whole process of treatment and resolving mental health issues? Let’s take a look.

If you look at some of the revered psychiatrists in India, you will notice their admancy to start with a thorough evaluation of their clients. This process includes noting all symptoms, reviewing medical history, conducting physical exams, and sometimes ordering lab tests.

Once a diagnosis is made, the treatment involves-

  • Managing symptoms through medications and interventions
  • Building psychotherapy interventions like CBT, DBT and REBT
  • Providing crisis management
  • Coordinating care with psychologists, counselors, and family doctors
  • Monitoring progress, adjusting medications or therapy as needed

In recent years, finding a good, reliable psychiatrist in India has become easier. Given the growth of mental health space in the country, the growth shift has been phenomenal. Urban areas, in particular, have seen a rise in psychiatric clinics, therapists and mental wellness centers.

With a key role in managing wellness in substance and alcohol abuse cases, psychiatrists hold a critical part. According to The Lancet Psychiatry, early psychiatric intervention, especially among young people, significantly reduces long-term mental health issues. Early intervention along with expert help is necessary for a quick & seamless recovery.

The role of a psychiatrist is critical in maintaining a fulfilled health. The Indian Journal of Psychiatry emphasizes that integrating psychiatrists into primary healthcare can enhance early diagnosis and treatment in India. Furthermore, this can prove as the basis for better intervention plans in the long run.

In short, a psychiatrist is not just someone who caters to specific mental health concerns. They are trained to support a wide range of issues and put necessary interventions into place.

At Tulasi Healthcare, we stand with you and provide the best support and environment needed to maintain a healthy life.

contentHtml:
Approach for mental health concerns by psychiatrist in india

Let us all be honest- mental health has finally started to get the attention it deserves. But seeking help always comes as an issue for many. There is an awareness, for sure, but that does not clearly mean that one will truly act on them. The urge to live a life of wellbeing shall come from within. With this in mind, taking insight from a reputed psychiatrist in India wil help us understand it better.

Let’s see how we can approach our mental health concerns in the right manner-

  • Acknowledge what you feel

It might sound like a very simple thing to do- but it has effects that measure beyond words. The fact that you know what you are going through- solves half the problem. Mental health concerns are not as black and white as they seem to us. There are a lot of perspectives to clear, and sitting with our thoughts helps us do the same.

  • Connect with your loved ones

Venting to your close, near and dear ones has a cathartic effect on our lives. Even if it’s a light hearted conversation, we feel energised and refreshed in moments. Sometimes, just saying things out loud makes a difference in our lives. Just sharing your feelings can start the journey of your wellness.

  • Consult a professional

An early intervention can have a huge impact on the level of resilience and wellbeing a person can sustain. According to the Indian Journal of Psychiatry, early interventions are key to promoting better treatment. It’s clear as day- don’t wait for a crisis to knock on your door! If you are unsure where to begin, consider conferring with Dr. Gorav Gupta, who is a very revered psychiatrist in India.

  • Stay consistent with self-care

When it comes to mental health, it isn’t about efforts once in a while. It’s a continuous process, where every step holds its importance. Sometimes, this attention to self-care is all one needs to get their lives back on track. This “self-care” acts as “Early intervention” when insight persits. So, sit with yourselves and make yourselves better each day!

  • Go easy on yourselves!

Kindness towards oneself definitely goes a long way. Looking into a paper published by The Lancet Psychiatry, the role of self-compassion in reducing anxiety and depression symptoms is essential. So, the next time an inner critic shows up for an audit, you know what to do!

Mental health isn’t a destination—it’s a journey towards stability. The right approach is the one where you are the priority, without any judgment or delay. So if your mind’s been waving red flags lately, take that as your sign to start the conversation, seek support, and remember: help is always available, and healing is possible.

excerpt: De-addiction is a process that goes beyond abstinence on a daily basis. It is a commitment that requires awareness and presence of mind. While medication has its own role to play, therapy has an efficacy that adds a human touch to healing. Different approaches like Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Dialectical Behavior Therapy and related interventions leave […]
contentHtml:
De-addiction is a process that goes beyond abstinence on a daily basis. It is a commitment that requires awareness and presence of mind. While medication has its own role to play, therapy has an efficacy that adds a human touch to healing. Different approaches like Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Dialectical Behavior Therapy and related interventions leave a great impact on the quality of caregiving.

These therapies as applied by some of the greatest psychiatrist in Delhi have a profound impact on the level of treatment efficacy. Let’s talk in further detail how these therapies have a major role in the journey of de-addiction.

  • Cognitive Behavioral Therapy– CBT is one of the most profoundly applied therapies, finding its way into treatment regimes as a staple. During de-addiction, it has a major role in keeping negative thoughts at bay and fostering a positive mindset. According to a study published in the American Journal of Psychiatry, CBT has proven to be a greatly effective method. It reduces long-time use by managing emotional regulation and fostering better decision making skills in the individual.
  • Dialectical Behavioral Therapy– DBT was first applied as a way to regulate mood in borderline personality issues. Through time, it has found its way in de-addiction treatment as well. This method integrates acceptance and change strategies, which allow clients to tolerate stress and handle emotions. As per a study in Journal of Substance Abuse Treatment, DBT enhances treatment retention and reduces drug frequency.
  • Motivational Interviewing– MI is an evidence based treatment that looks into the mindset of the client to pursue treatment. It enhances the individual’s readiness to change and fosters a sense of internal motivation. When combined with CBT & DBT, MI has often proven to be a great intervention. If you approach Tulasi Healthcare for your de-addiction concerns, it can be a great step towards your mental wellbeing.
  • Contingency Management– In this method, positive reinforcement is used as a strategy to enhance abstinence. It has shown great short term outcomes in stimulant and opioid users.

In general, applying therapeutic management during de-addiction treatment can work wonders, especially in the long run. If you feel you should confer with an expert, connecting with a good psychiatrist in Delhi if you are a resident can be a good option.

Remember, therapy in de-addiction is not a one-size-fits-all model but a personalized journey. Connect with professionals today and explore options towards your well being.

title: Adult ADHD
h1: Adult ADHD
excerpt: What is attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) Attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is one of the most common childhood and adolescent neuropsychiatric disorders. It was once perceived as a neurodevelopmental disorder meaning it was first diagnosed in childhood and would resolve by adolescence or early adulthood but it is now recognised as lifespan […]
contentHtml:
What is attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)

Attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is one of the most common childhood and adolescent neuropsychiatric disorders. It was once perceived as a neurodevelopmental disorder meaning it was first diagnosed in childhood and would resolve by adolescence or early adulthood but it is now recognised as lifespan neurodevelopmental disorder and its manifestations in adults are widely recognised. Multiple studies have concluded that majority of school age children diagnosed with ADHD continues to have clinically significant symptoms and impairments into young adulthood. Both children and adults suffer significantly with psychiatric comorbidities and neurocognitive deficits, but adults have more functional impairment.

Adult ADHD has a prevalence of around 4.4 % and yet remains under-recognised and untreated. It has high prevalence of secondary comorbid mental illness like mood disorder, substance use disorder, learning disabilities, poor interpersonal relationships, academic and occupational impairments. As a consequence these may lead to unemployement, financial troubles, troubles with the law, unstable relationships, poor self image, poor physical and mental health and road traffic accidents. They also have higher rates of divorce and separation, affecting the quality of life of the individual.

All these negative consequences warrants for identification and treatment of the illness.

Common symptoms of adult ADHD

Common symptoms of adult ADHD includes carelessness, inaccurate work, difficulty in sustaining focus on boring work, troubles with extensive reading, difficulty in retaining information, problems with following direction or finishing tasks, procrastinating, missing deadlines, misplacing things, easily distracted by surrounding noises, fidgety or restlessness, louder than normal, finishes others sentences or answering before question is completed, difficulty in waiting, interrupts others in conversations.

If these symptoms are present on occasions and do not have significant impact on your life minor modifications in lifestyle may help but in case they starts disrupting life of an individual a professional help should be sort. Diagnosing adult ADHD may be difficult as it may appear like other mental illness like mood disorder (mania, depression), anxiety.

Treatment

Medications/pharmacotherapy remains the cornerstone of the treatment which includes stimulant and non stimulants. Stimulants are the most commonly used medications although, due to risk of abuse or illicit diversion of these medications clinicians feel reluctant in prescribing these medications. Strong evidence has been found for Cognitive behaviour therapy (both in individual and group settings). Other approaches such as ADHD coaching, yoga, mindfulness training, cognitive remediation programs, neurofeedback etc have also been found helpful. Personalised management plan according to the needs of the patient are best, for eg couples therapy for individuals suffering from marital or relationship discord. Education planning, consideration of academic and occupation accommodations are of utmost importance as part of the treatment which would involve occupational counselling and vocational training rather than insisting on a long term (3-4 years college/course).

contentHtml:
Recovery is a journey that is full of constant upgrades and setbacks. Relapse is one such stage that anyone in recovery can encounter. However sudden it may be, there are always early signs that indicate its presence. Recognizing these signs lead professionals to a timely intervention, and hence maintaining a life of wellbeing. Tulasi Healthcare takes advanced steps in helping its clients at bay from relapse. With an expert team under some of the best psychiatrist in Delhi, we facilitate some of the best resources the mental health fraternity has to offer.

Let’s take a look at what small changes can be noticed to keep relapse at bay!

  • Increasing mood irritability

Sudden mood changes are a quick giveaway of the person’s mental status. These emotional shifts add to the craving of addictive substances and should not be overlooked. If the client is maintaining this mood, it is advisable to take them to their consultant and get necessary intervention.

  • Social Withdrawal

After a successful recovery, a person is truly facilitated and equipped to go back to society. Isolation is a clear sign of upcoming mental health issues, and some caregivers mistake it as a need to refuel and attain mindfulness. This sign should receive proper intervention and enquiry to keep doubts at bay.

  • Sleep Disturbances

Sleep disturbances are an instant sign of trouble with mental health issues. Constant sleep disruptions are early signs of relapse and oncoming depression and anxiety. For keeping it at bay, healthy lifestyle choices should be made at every point. Such interjections can only come when a consultation is made. If you reside in the national capital and are looking for a psychiatrist in Delhi, Tulasi Healthcare can be your guide.

  • Neglecting Personal Hygiene

Personal Hygiene is the boldest mark of mental health stability. An unkempt, haphazard and noticeable decline in self-care routines is a clear sign of impending relapse. Such signs may seem normal on occasions, but should not be left out of watch. A keen eye on the part of caregivers goes a long way to help in such cases.

  • Appetite changes

Appetite and lifestyle changes are a crucial part of determining if a person is going through some mental health concern. Monitoring this particular shift is a great way to provide timely intervention.

  • Feelings of hopelessness

Feeling lost and hopeless is a clear sign that a mental health issue is at play. Such persistent feelings are a prompt indication towards self harm or indulging in depreciating activities. These small instigations lead to relapse without much required.

If you notice these signs in yourself or a loved one, it’s essential to consult a mental health professional. Early intervention can prevent a full-blown relapse and facilitate a return to stability. Dr. Gorav Gupta can be an excellent resource person to consult with in cases of relapse. With his experience of 2 decades, he has brought about a change in mental health treatment.

contentHtml:
The thought of considering going to a psychiatrist is far-fetched even today in most Indian households. Even while facing problems of multiple magnitudes, it is seen that many of us are hesitant to seek actual help. However, when do these feelings become more than just a passing phase, and when should you seek professional help? At what point does one consider seeing a psychiatrist? This is where we come in. As an active community of mental health focused individuals, we fuel what we do best- awareness towards mental health. Seeing such questions floating in social spaces helps us consider the needs of individuals. So, as one of the best psychiatrist in Delhi, Dr Gorav Gupta facilitates such write ups to bring about awareness in the community. With this in mind, let’s discuss why and when you can consider seeing a psychiatrist.

Understanding the role of a psychiatrist

A psychiatrist is a medical professional who specializes in diagnosing, treating, and preventing mental health conditions. Unlike therapists, psychiatrists are trained doctors with expertise in both the biological and psychological aspects of mental health. They can prescribe medication, offer therapy, and help individuals manage complex emotional, psychological, and behavioral issues. 

If you are a resident of in and around Delhi who is considering visiting a psychiatrist, this blog is your key. With an amalgamation of holistic therapies, non-traditional therapies and  board of experts, Tulasi Health Care is the place to be. As a renowned psychiatrist in Delhi, Dr. Gorav’s expertise is unparalleled in the field of mental health. 

Seeking help is crucial- Tulasi Healthcare can be your solution.

What is the first stage of mental breakdown?

The first stage of a mental breakdown often goes unnoticed as usual stress and anxiety related to daily tasks. Then, it gradually escalates to chronic stress and emotional exhaustion. You might feel constantly overwhelmed, anxious, or irritable, struggling to concentrate or sleep. 

Small tasks feel impossible, and emotions swing unpredictably, leading to disbalance in life. Ignoring these early signs can make things worse over time. If you’re in this phase, seeking help early is key. A professional can help you understand what’s happening and how to manage it. If you’re looking for support, consulting a psychiatrist in Delhi can be a great step toward recovery. 

What are the 5 early warning signs of mental illness?

Early warning signs are the best way to assess and provide an intervention at developing stages. Here, if information is present and applied in the right way, a person can save tons of effort and energy to restore their mental health.

Let’s explore how a top psychiatrist in Delhi can guide you to understand these signs- 

  • Persistent sadness or anxiety – Feeling low majority of the times and being constantly worried without a clear reason.
  • Mood swings – Extreme highs and lows in emotional capacity that affect daily life and decisions.
  • Social withdrawal – Avoiding friends, family, social circles or activities once enjoyed. Distancing oneself from any kind of interaction.
  • Changes in sleep or appetite –Experiencing insomnia or hypersomnia, sudden weight loss or gain that is unaccounted for.
  • Difficulty concentrating – Struggling to focus, remember things, or make decisions.

If you notice these signs and reside in Delhi, reaching out to a top psychiatrist in Delhi like Dr Gorav Gupta can help. Early intervention makes a big difference!

What are some inherent warning signs?

It is essential to know when you need to consult a psychiatrist. Some signs are clear indications- but others might not be. As responsible professionals, our aim is to raise awareness amongst our readers to identify issues and seek help. Let’s understand some crucial points-

Difficulty managing emotions–

  • Feeling overwhelmed and out of control is a sign that can indicate towards seeking help. It can happen to someone eventually, but if it is occurring on a regular basis, it’s time to ask for guidance. It can be challenging to manage emotions if they feel intense or unpredictable. As a good psychiatrist in Delhi, we aim to raise awareness amongst all.

Substance abuse-

  • Casual use of addictive substances is often used as a coping mechanism amongst many. This masks the long term effect of stress in and brewing issues in many ways, thus misleading individuals to mask their issues. Substance abuse and self-harm are often symptoms of deeper psychological struggles such as depression, trauma, or anxiety disorders. A psychiatrist can help you address the underlying causes of these behaviors and provide support to break unhealthy cycles.

Social withdrawal & thoughts of self harm-

  • Social withdrawal serves as a present sign that an individual is facing issues with their mental health. They try to cope with their issues in isolation, trying to understand what they can do to make it better. This deteriorates their condition further and leads to thoughts of self harm and depression. If you are looking for a  good psychiatrist in Delhi, they can provide therapy to help you address these feelings. They can teach you techniques to engage with others, and support you in re-establishing social connections that improve your well-being.

What to expect while visiting a psychiatrist?

Visiting a psychiatrist might feel overwhelming at first, but it is the start of a big and positive journey. The first step is typically an initial assessment, where your psychiatrist will gather information. This will include your symptoms, medical history, and any potential triggers for your mental health struggles. After that, it is all about proper diagnosis and a journey that is packed with positive actions. 

During your sessions, our team of best psychiatrist in Delhi may recommend a combination of therapy and medication. Stabilizing the current issues while planning for a long term recovery is the course of action.

Connect with the top psychiatrist in Delhi today!

Approaching a psychiatrist these days is not a stigma, but a necessity in today’s lifestyle. Even with tons of awareness campaigns, normalization at the grassroot level takes its own time. Through continuous efforts and progress, Tulasi Healthcare has built a team of top psychiatrists to guide individuals in their mental health journey. 

To know more on how our team can assist you, connect with us through www.tulasihealthcare.com today!

Delving into what we face we learn and gain on a daily basis from our clients. So, let’s understand what being a mental health practitioner is all about. This blog will delve into the various ways a psychiatrist can offer support. Particularly for those searching for a good psychiatrist in Delhi, this is a must read.

We will discuss how a psychiatrist can aid you as an individual suffering from a mental health crisis. 

Who is a Psychiatrist?

You must have heard this word on many platforms, which is often confused with a psychologist or a counsellor. Well, the names may be different, but the goal remains the same- aid the clients to live their best. 

In general, a psychiatrist is an individual specializing in diagnosing, treating, and preventing mental health disorders. Unlike therapists or counselors, psychiatrists are medical doctors who can prescribe medication in addition to providing psychotherapy. Psychiatrists have extensive training in both the biological and psychological aspects of mental health. This makes them uniquely equipped to offer a comprehensive approach to treatment.

When seeking help from a psychiatrist in Delhi, you may be surprised by the range of services available. From medication management to psychotherapy, and even lifestyle recommendations to improve overall mental well-being.

With this in mind, you must wonder how a team of psychiatrists at Tulasi healthcare aid you in your mental well being? Well, we have listed an accumulation of our services. We work in a broad spectrum to help our clients with their issues.

What is the Benefit of Seeing a Psychiatrist?

Seeing a psychiatrist offers several benefits, particularly for individuals dealing with mental health challenges that may require professional intervention. A psychiatrist provides a holistic approach to mental health, addressing both the biological and psychological aspects of mental health issues. By offering expert guidance and treatment, psychiatrists can significantly improve a person’s emotional well-being, helping them lead a more balanced and fulfilling life.

How do I know I need a Psychiatrist?

You may need to see a psychiatrist if you’re experiencing persistent mental health symptoms that are interfering with your daily life. The signs to look for can include-

  • – Lasting feelings of sadness or hopelessness
  • – Overwhelming Anxiety
  • – Severe Mood Swings
  • – Difficulty Coping with Everyday Tasks
  • – Withdrawing from Social Activities
  • – Struggling to Manage Relationships & Work responsibilities
  • – Engaging in Self-Destructive Behaviors

Types of Issues where a Psychiatrist can help

A psychiatrist’s expertise is vast in nature, and they can help with a variety of mental health conditions. These include-

Anxiety Treatment

From mild feelings of nervousness to severe panic attacks, anxiety can manifest in a variety of ways. A psychiatrist can help you understand the causes of your anxiety and develop a treatment plan tailored to your needs. Medication, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), is often prescribed to manage symptoms. In addition, therapy can help you develop coping strategies and reduce the intensity of anxious feelings.

Depression

It is a condition that is widely recognized and has impacted many. When it comes to depression, it often leaves individuals feeling hopeless, disconnected, and exhausted. With a therapeutic and medicinal integration through the best psychiatrist in Delhi, you can be assured of the best treatment. Medication can help balance brain chemistry, while therapy can provide strategies for managing negative thoughts and emotions. 

Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD)

A pattern of obsessive and intrusive behaviors, OCD can be a debilitating condition to deal with. This cycle is quite stressful and many cannot even comprehend how to deal with this situation. Dr. Gorav Gupta is  the top psychiatrist in Delhi specializing in dealing with cases of OCD and its management strategies. CBT, Exposure therapy and other non-traditional treatments are also a source of management when OCD reaches a severe level.

Bipolar Disorder

Characterized by the presence of mood swings, the range can be on extremities depending upon the situation the client is facing. Psychiatrists treat bipolar disorder with mood-stabilizing medications and therapy. It is used along with therapeutic intervention to aid a long term stability and well being for clients.

Schizophrenia

A serious issue, Schizophrenia is a condition that slips out of diagnosis and is one of the highest misdiagnosed conditions. It is a serious disorder that affects how a person thinks, feels, and behaves. People with schizophrenia often experience hallucinations and delusions that hinder their daily activities and wellbeing. Suggested course of treatment is usually a medication and counselling based approach, where the progress is strictly monitored. As a top psychiatrist in Delhi, Dr. Gorav Gupta boasts a team of experts that align such issues with ease.

Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)

PTSD is a condition that develops when a person encounters a deep trauma, abuse or loss.  A psychiatrist can help those with PTSD. by offering trauma-focused therapy and medications. This helps control anxiety and mood swings that often accompany the condition.

How can a Psychiatrist Help?

Assessment & Diagnosis

The first step is typically an assessment for confirming the present and reported symptoms. If you are thinking of consulting a psychiatrist in Delhi, approaching Tulasi Healthcare can be a good bet. There, you will be asked about your medical history, symptoms, and any significant life events that could have contributed to your mental health issues. This assessment is crucial for an accurate diagnosis.

Personalized Treatment Plan

Once a clear diagnosis is made, having a personalized treatment plan is essential.  This plan could include medication, psychotherapy, lifestyle adjustments, or a combination of all three. A good psychiatrist will work closely with a team of experts. This helps build a plan that is suited and tailored according to the client’s needs.

Treatment Management

Apart from a personalized plan, it needs a keen eye to take upon the task of managing. With medications, therapies and holistic activities it’s hard to see what is working for the client. With a team of good psychiatrist in Delhi, we assure that everyone receives the best of care.

Crisis Management

Psychiatrists offer immediate support during crises. Providing coping mechanisms, advice, and sometimes hospitalization or other interventions to stabilize the situation. With our emergency services, anyone can approach us anytime to avail the best mental health interventions.

The importance of Finding the Right Psychiatrist

It takes a keen eye to spot what works the best for you. As the team of top psychiatrist in Delhi, we take it upon ourselves to safeguard the interests of our clients. 

A good psychiatrist not only has the necessary qualifications and experience but also fosters a supportive relationship with you. Look for someone who listens attentively, communicates effectively, and works with you to create a treatment that meets your needs.

Don’t hesitate to reach out for help.

title: What is Alzehimer’s disease? How can we treat & manage it?
h1: What is Alzheimer’s disease? How can we treat & manage it?
excerpt: What is Alzheimer’s disease? How can we treat & manage it? Alzheimer’s is a disorder that tends to take on millions of people around the world. It is a progressive, brain degenerative disorder. It usually leads to significant changes in behavior and hampers everyday functioning of an individual. With an aging population, Alzheimer’s has become […]
contentHtml:
Alzheimer’s is a disorder that tends to take on millions of people around the world. It is a progressive, brain degenerative disorder. It usually leads to significant changes in behavior and hampers everyday functioning of an individual. With an aging population, Alzheimer’s has become a global issue with limited resources to manage it. It is definitely one of the most problematic concerns worldwide and needs awareness around it.  For the exploration of its treatment, it is necessary.

As Tulasi, we take it upon ourselves to make people aware about it and discuss different aspects of Alzheimer’s. Today we discuss what it is, Alzheimer treatment, and ways to manage the disease effectively. Additionally, we will discuss the role of Alzheimer care facilities and Alzheimer patient care homes in supporting those living with the condition.

What exactly is Alzheimer’s?

First identified in 1906, Alzheimer’s is a degenerative brain disease that is characterized by the accumulation of amyloid plaques and tau tangles in the brain.

What do these particular structures do? One might wonder. Simply put, these structures break the communication between nerve cells, leading to brain cell death and the gradual loss of cognitive functions. Primarily, it is marked by symptoms like memory loss, confusion in daily decisions and tasks, difficulty with speech formation and understanding, impaired judgment, and sudden mood changes. 

Age is a marked factor for development of Alzheimer’s; but not a definitive one. People under 65 may also develop it given a higher genetic risk factor. 

Symptoms & Diagnosis 

The progression of Alzheimer’s comes in stages, becoming more pronounced with time. In early stages, the symptoms are not very recognizable, but show up in a few moments, tasks and lapses of decision making that are not easily noticed. 

As the disease advances, individuals may struggle with familiar tasks, have difficulty recognizing loved ones, and experience significant changes in personality and behavior.

Common signs and symptoms of Alzheimer’s disease include:

  • Memory loss-

  • The person starts to forget their daily routines, gets confused with easy tasks and cannot remember details that are of common knowledge to them.

  • Confusion with familiar things-

  • The person feels confusion between things that have always been present for them.

  • Difficulty with language & pronunciation-

  • Trouble recalling words or repeating the same phrases

  • Faulty judgement-

  • The people with Alzheimer’s face issues in making the right decisions since they cannot remember information required to make proper judgement.

  • Mood changes-

  • Increased anxiety, depression, or irritability persists without any particular cause. 

  • Disorientation-

  • There is a loss of time, space and surroundings and the person feels lost in familiar places.

The diagnosis for Alzheimer’s although, has no particular tests that can clearly define its diagnosis. A team of experts can perform a variety of exams that can include psychological assessments, neurological imaging (PET, CT) and cognitive exams to confirm suspicions for Alzheimer’s. Blood tests and other lab work may also be conducted to exclude other medical conditions that might mimic Alzheimer’s symptoms. 

Alzheimer Treatments: What to expect?

Even with revolutionary biological and technological advancements in the last few decades, there is no cure for Alzheimer’s. At present, only medication, therapy, lifestyle changes, and care support are some of the ways to manage and maintain an acceptable quality of life for these individuals. 

Medicinal interventions for Alzheimer’s as per FDA approval are listed below-

  • Glutamate regulators:

  • Learning and memory in the human brain is associated with a neurotransmitter called Glutamate, which is regulated by a regulator called Memantine. With the help of Memantine, the overstimulation of brain cells is soothed and used in combination with Cholinesterase inhibitors for moderate to severe Alzheimer’s.

  • Cholinesterase inhibitors:

  • Acetylcholine is another important neurotransmitter that is usually found in depleted conditions in Alzheimer’s patients. To regulate these, cholinesterase inhibitors like Donepezil, Rivastigmine, and Galantamine are used. They temporarily restore memory and cognitive functions.

In 2021, the FDA also approved Aduhelm, a new drug designed to target amyloid plaques in the brain. While its approval has been controversial, it represents a potential new avenue in Alzheimer disease treatment.

Non- Pharmacological interventions employed in Alzheimer Treatments-

Apart from interventions at Medical level, therapeutic treatments are also available to manage the condition of Alzheimer’s. Cognitive stimulation therapy (CST), reality orientation therapy (ROT), and other types of cognitive rehabilitation may help patients maintain their abilities for a longer period. Apart from these, speech therapy, physical therapy and occupational therapy helps clients to be active in all regards and face everyday challenges of practical life. 

Lifestyle changes & Management

Lifestyle is a crucial part when it comes to chronic conditions. It defines the level of care and management one needs to sustain a healthy lifestyle.

For a good management, these steps can be taken-

  • Alzheimer Care Facilities & Alzheimer Patient Care Homes

When the disease progresses to a certain extent, Alzheimer patients require 24/7 care that a homely environment is not able to provide. For this particular reason Alzheimer Care Facilities & Alzheimer Patient Care Homes like Tulasi Healthcare exist. These facilities house professionals that are trained to deal with chronic mental health issues and provide an environment of wellbeing. 

If you are searching for an Alzheimer care center near me and landed on this piece of info, you are at the right place. Tulasi Healthcare can help you with this difficult decision & consider factors such as location, staff qualifications, the facility’s approach to care, and the environment when making this choice.

  • Caregiver support

 Through respite care, counseling, & community resources, caregiver support can be provided to many suffering from the burnout of caring for their loved ones. Family members may also benefit from joining Alzheimer’s support groups, where they can share experiences and learn from others facing similar challenges.

Looking ahead: Future of Alzheimer Treatment

Moving forward, we hope this blog can be a great reference for you and your loved ones to choose the right kind of management plan. The journey is surely difficult, given the circumstances and situation people with Alzheimer’s might have to face. Keeping this in mind, we at Tulasi Healthcare make sure that we provide the best of abilities and service to everyone who comes to us with a problem. 

While the journey may be difficult, it is important to remember that Alzheimer’s patients can lead fulfilling lives with the right treatment and care in place.

title: Geriatric therapy: How to help aging adults with mental health issues?
h1: Geriatric therapy: How to help aging adults with mental health issues?
excerpt: As one starts to age, there are issues that life throws at us that cannot be avoided. The life of an older adult can be quite isolating and difficult. Their health, mindset and living conditions can severely impact their mindset. From the grief of losing loved ones to the difficulty of adjusting to retirement, senior […]
contentHtml:
As one starts to age, there are issues that life throws at us that cannot be avoided. The life of an older adult can be quite isolating and difficult. Their health, mindset and living conditions can severely impact their mindset. From the grief of losing loved ones to the difficulty of adjusting to retirement, senior years bring unique stressors. It becomes crucial to understand their mindset. So, for such individuals geriatric therapy has been developed as a different branch of psychology. At this stage of life development, one needs wisdom, support and unconditional regard for their emotions. It can be instrumental in supporting mental health for older adults.

In today’s discussion, we explore the importance of geriatric therapy, focusing on elderly mental health treatment, senior psychotherapy, and different types of therapeutic interventions for older adults.

What is Geriatric Therapy?

Geriatric behavioral therapy is a specialized form of mental health therapy that focuses on addressing the psychological needs of older adults. It looks into the age specific problems that arise on a social, emotional and psychological level. If you look into mental health services for seniors, you will find a wide range of services that cater to their psychological, physical and adjustment needs.

As per our observations and expertise, At Tulasi Healthcare we have noticed the severity and diversity of different issues that persist on older adults. Let’s take a quick look.

Important numbers in Geriatric Therapy

Mental health services for seniors are going to be an integral part of India’s psychological care landscape. Around 20.5% of older adults in India suffer from mental health issues, which translates to approximately 17.13 million seniors. Despite this, geriatric therapy services remain inadequate, with many relying on general healthcare providers to gain insight on their condition.

The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE) aims to address these issues, but implementation and accessibility remain challenges in rural and remote areas. At Tulasi Healthcare, our dedicated geriatric psychiatry program helps elders gain the support and insight they need into their issues.

Common issues in Geriatric counseling services

There is a range of mental health issues that plagues older adults, which include-

  • Depression– This is one of the highest reported issues when it comes to geriatric counseling. At this stage, individuals start experiencing feelings of isolation, loss, or chronic illness. It can affect their energy, appetite, sleep and overall interaction with their loved ones.
  • Anxiety– Approaching the near end of their lives, some older adults may experience anxiety about their future. Usually, their health, finances and family matters are the key issues. To tackle this, elderly anxiety treatment can be employed to reduce fear of the unknown and build a hope in their lives.
  • Cognitive decline- Cognitive issues are the source of multiple problems in old age. Problems like Alzehimer’s, Dementia and Parkinson’s are primarily cognitive in nature, they can also result in depression, anxiety, and frustration, requiring specialized care.
  • Grief & Loss- As people age, they often lose their loved ones, friends, & even see a deterioration in their own health. Grieving these losses can contribute to sadness and emotional pain, which can lead to depression.
  • Social Isolation- With retirement, separate living situations and family moving away, older adults may feel isolated. This can lead to isolation and resulting mental health issues.

With these issues at hand, understanding different counseling and therapies that can be used in such cases is essential. Let’s go through various therapies and methods that can be employed to manage the symptoms and provide a ray of hope and happiness to older adults.

Geriatric Counseling Services: A personalized approach

Geriatric counseling services adopt a holistic approach, setting personalized standards for each case. Whether the treatment includes therapy or counseling sessions, the main aim is to provide emotional support and equip individuals to deal with constant changes in their lives.

  • Individual therapy– Here, a geriatric counselor will be involved in a closed setting exploring the client’s history, pressing concerns and draw a treatment plan. . This is an excellent option for seniors dealing with grief, loneliness, or depression.
  • Family & Group therapy– Family dynamics play an important role in addressing concerns in the life of older adults. Some geriatric counseling services like Tulasi Healthcare also offer group therapy, where seniors can interact with others experiencing similar challenges. This helps reduce feelings of isolation and offers a sense of community.

Therapeutic, Psychiatric & Medical interventions

  • CBT & Senior Depression Therapy– CBT is a great way to tackle anxiety and depression in older adults. Since it is a talk and intervention based therapy, it helps them identify and change negative thought patterns and behaviors. CBT for elderly anxiety treatment is also a great option to consider for underlying issues.

In cases of senior depression therapy, techniques like person centered approach and supportive measures can be employed.

  • Medical interventions- Geriatric psychiatry deals with prescription of medication and monitoring its effects. This needs critical focus since aged individuals may react differently to varied dosages.
  • Psychiatric interventions– Cognitive assessments are a critical part of diagnosis and treatment. These assessments help determine if cognitive issues are contributing to mental health problems. This is especially important in cases of dementia or Alzheimer’s disease.
  • Behavioral Interventions– Along with mindfulness and relaxation, social engagement and physical rehabilitation play a very important part during behavior interventions.These techniques are particularly helpful for seniors dealing with chronic pain or health concerns. At Tulasi Healthcare, we focus on a holistic and comprehensive care plan by employing these interventions with a geriatric counselor.

Connect with Tulasi Healthcare for Geriatric Therapy today.

As the population increases, access to mental health services for seniors takes priority for us as a society. By understanding the gaps, issues and therapeutic interventions for seniors, we can create a safe space for a growing community. At Tulasi Healthcare, our team of dedicated professionals prioritize senior mental health and ensure that our older adults have access to the help they need to thrive.

Connect with us today for a therapy session for your loved ones at www.tulasihealthcare.com

title: How Rehabilitation Centers Tailor Treatment Plans for Individual Needs- debunking myths
h1: How Rehabilitation Centers Tailor Treatment Plans for Individual Needs- debunking myths
excerpt: A rehabilitation center is a place of healing, comfort and support for many. When clients come and see us at our facility, we are always left puzzled with a particular statement- ‘ Will our loved ones be kept locked in and not allowed to meet anybody? Will they be treated well?’ Such myths, misconceptions and […]
contentHtml:
A rehabilitation center is a place of healing, comfort and support for many.

When clients come and see us at our facility, we are always left puzzled with a particular statement- ‘ Will our loved ones be kept locked in and not allowed to meet anybody? Will they be treated well?’

Such myths, misconceptions and inhumane mindsets are a thing of the past. Our rehabilitation centre in Delhi is all about treating people with mental health conditions more sensitively, putting in extra effort into their care and concerns.

At Tulasi healthcare, we make sure that every individual receives specialized attention, is treated fairly and cared for in the best manner.

Let’s explore some common myths, misconceptions and our strategies of treatment which are applied to provide relief and comfort to our clients.

Myth1- Only people with severe addiction go to rehabilitation centres

Reality– Well, this is not true! At our Delhi Rehab center, we encounter many cases daily that are related to several things. It can be stress and burnout from financial or work life balance, some mental health condition or simply cases of addiction that require intervention.

These issues are not solitary, but can also be quite inter-related. So this myth is quite different than what is seen in reality.

On the contrary, if the cases of addiction that are just at mild and moderate level approach our facility, it is a gamechanger to their treatment. As the best rehabilitation centre in Delhi NCR, we have always maintained awareness and support in such matters and provided critical and emergency care to our clients.

Myth 2- When you go to the rehab, you’ll be cured forever!

Reality- There is a certain ‘notion’ that when a person goes into a rehabilitation centre, they will come out “brand new”, as per many!

Well, it is a myth that definitely needs to be addressed. Recovery from addiction or mental health conditions is a lifelong journey. It takes continuous efforts from every end- the client, their caregivers and rehab center facility to keep a track of their recovery and progress. After completing a rehabilitation program, many individuals continue with outpatient therapy, support groups, or other aftercare services. Maintaining a lifestyle that is free from triggers and adapting self management is the key. It only ensures successful treatment in the long run!

Myth 3- A Rehabilitation centre is full of violent and untrusted people.

Reality- This is one of the widely reported myths that our clients’ caregivers usually ask us.

“Will our loved ones be safe? Will they be alright?”

We hear these on a daily basis. So addressing this issue is vital.

Our rehabilitation centre in Delhi is a controlled and safe environment. Before we take any steps, we make sure to gauge the client’s condition and make arrangements accordingly. If the client is indeed in a condition where he can harm self and others, they are taken into solitary confinement and monitored till their condition improves.

Myth 4- A rehab center is expensive for most people.

title: Is dementia curable?
h1: Is dementia curable?
excerpt: Dementia has emerged as an emerging issue amongst the Indian masses. Given its ambiguous rise and development, many of us fail to discover its true presentation, and how one can manage it properly. At Tulasi, we are approached by many clients asking for a cure, but it takes more than just a cure to control […]
contentHtml:
Dementia has emerged as an emerging issue amongst the Indian masses. Given its ambiguous rise and development, many of us fail to discover its true presentation, and how one can manage it properly. At Tulasi, we are approached by many clients asking for a cure, but it takes more than just a cure to control dementia. With continuous advancements, medicinal interventions have taken a step ahead. But even with these, a total cure is yet to be found. Dementia affects millions of people globally, with the World Health Organization estimating that approximately 55 million people worldwide are living with dementia.

As of now, the scientific consensus is clear: dementia is not currently curable. However, this does not mean that there is no hope. Treatment options exist that can manage symptoms, slow progression, and improve quality of life for those affected. In this blog, we’ll explore the nature of dementia, current treatment options, ongoing research, and the potential for a cure in the future.

Why isn’t dementia curable- yet?

There are certain factors to account for when it comes to a complex condition like dementia. Even with advancements and widespread access, its a challenging task. With amazing tech and experts available for dementia treatment in Delhi NCR itself, let’s discuss why approaching a cure is still a mystery to human kind.

  • Complexity of brain structures- Human brain is incredibly complex, with billions and trillions of neurons connecting with each other. With a web of interconnected functions and delicate structures understanding the mechanism behind each can be quite a task.

Neurodegeneration has a variety of issues related to it, and tracing it back to its original roots is not an option available even with modern machinery. Each dementia has its own characteristic, which we explore with our dementia treatment in delhi NCR.

  • Late diagnosis- Till the time the issue is discovered, significant damage is done. By the time symptoms become apparent, brain damage has already occurred, and treatment options become limited. Early detection is critical to developing effective treatments, but as of now, diagnosing dementia in its earliest stages remains difficult.
  • Lack of information- There are many forms of dementia that are not clearly understood even now. For example, while scientists know that Alzheimer’s disease involves the buildup of amyloid plaques and tau tangles in the brain, the exact mechanisms that lead to this buildup are not completely clear. This lack of understanding makes it harder to develop treatments that can stop or reverse the process.
  • Lack of clinical trials- Without much advancements, clinical trials are scarce. Many drugs have either shown limited effect or problems related to excessive side effects, which complicates the search for an effective cure.
  • Genetic and environmental concerns- With a no one size fits all plan, there are numerous genetic, environmental and lifestyle factors that contribute to the situation. Even certain management plans may not be suitable for everyone. That is why your best bet can be seeking dementia treatment in Delhi NCR for best management plans.

Treatment options for dementia in Delhi NCR

The current methods put in place can provide a significant level of management. Even with those in place, treatment is a far cry. For now, many management options are available that can improve quality of life with an increased life span in place.

  • Medical intervention- Medical interventions provide a way to stabilize the symptoms in a fast progressing condition like dementia. Antidepressants, antipsychotics, and mood stabilizers may be prescribed to manage symptoms like depression, anxiety, agitation, or aggression, though they are used cautiously due to potential side effects. Cholinesterase inhibitors are also used to increase the levels of acetylcholine, which aid in memory and learning.
  • Cognitive Stimulation Therapy- CST therapies provide a way to engage in problem solving activities that stimulate memory and jog cognitive activities. While CST doesn’t cure dementia, it can help maintain cognitive function and provide a sense of purpose and enjoyment for individuals with dementia.
  • Physical activity- Regular physical activity has been shown to have a positive effect on brain health. Exercise can help improve memory and cognitive function in the early stages of dementia and may also have an impact on reducing the risk of developing dementia in the first place.
  • Diet and nutrition- Diet is a crucial part of keeping neurodegenerative conditions at bay. Diets rich in antioxidants, healthy fats, and anti-inflammatory foods may help support brain health.

Future possibilities for treatment

Researchers are actively keeping records of therapy and advancements in the field.

  • Gene therapy- Advancements in genetic therapy can pave the way towards a cure for dementia. Researchers are studying how certain genes contribute to the development of dementia and whether targeting these genes could slow or stop the disease.With a breakthrough, this can prove as a potential treatment in the times to come.
  • Immunotherapy- Immunotherapy acts as a way of exploring ways to reduce potential inflammation in the brain. With a clean immune system, the body can fight harmful cells and build a defense on its own. Early trials in this area have shown some promise, though much more research is needed before these therapies become widely available.
  • Stem cell therapy- Stem cell therapy has previously shown promise in regenerating and providing a new life to many areas of the body. Keeping the same principle in place, stem cell therapy can also be used in regenerating lost brain cells and even replacing lost neurons. While this technology is still in its infancy, it could one day offer a way to regenerate the brain and reverse some of the damage caused by dementia.

What ways to explore?

Is there a cure for now? The answer remains no. But with certain advancements and current management strategies in place, we can surely say the hope remains strong. With Tulasi Home’s amazing facilities and 24/7 services that cater to the needs of your loved one’s, we are sure to be your clear choice for unfettered support. The journey towards living a well-maintained life in dementia can be difficult, but not an impossible feat. To know how we can help you during this journey, connect with us today.
